The custodian households that remain are gathered into seven houses, each answerable to the vein-house for its share of the coal and of the measured burning: Clann Mhuirich, Clann Fhearchair, Clann Ìomhair, Clann Raghnaill, Clann Thormoid, Clann Choinnich and Clann Lachlainn. Here for the first time the right to the coal passes by house and not by apprenticeship.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-2522"><em>The sitting on the seven kindreds argued two days</em>, 27 an t-Samhain, LE 54</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0035"></a>**28 an t-Iuchar, LE 55** — *Death of Queen Beathag* (Cathair dhearg). Queen Beathag nic Dhòmhnaill dies at Cathair dhearg, the last ruler of Dia-thìr who saw the fleet. Her son Raghnall mac Uilleim is crowned in the same hall.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EIV-1518"><em>Birth of Raghnall mac Uilleim</em>, 18 an t-Samhain, LE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-2523"></a>**28 an t-Sultain, LE 55** — *Na Seachd Taighean sworn* (Muileann dhearg). Taigh na Fèithe gathers the remaining custodian households into seven kindreds large enough to answer for a share of the galleries between them: Clann Mhuirich, Clann Fhearchair, Clann Ìomhair, Clann Raghnaill, Clann Thormoid, Clann Choinnich and Clann Lachlainn. Their seven heads are sworn before Crom's stone, and the right to the coal passes from that year by house and no longer by apprenticeship alone.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0034"><em>The seven houses of custody</em>, 4 an t-Iuchar, LE 55</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-2524"></a>**17 an Dàmhair, LE 55** — *Donnchadh writes Mionnan nan Seachd heads* (Muileann dhearg). Donnchadh mac Thormoid enters the seven heads' oath into Leabhar a' Chùraim in the same plain hand he has kept his whole working life, and finds himself thinking less of Lagh an Loscaidh Bhig than of the fifth of hands the sitting never once named aloud: those fifteen years and a whole sea away, on a shore the book has no line to enter them against.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0034"><em>The seven houses of custody</em>, 4 an t-Iuchar, LE 55</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-2525"></a>**23 an Dàmhair, LE 55** — *Death of Beathag nic Dhòmhnaill at seventy-six* (Cathair dhearg). Queen Beathag nic Dhòmhnaill dies at Cathair dhearg in the summer, seventy and six years old, after one-and-sixty years upon An Talla Dearg's floor, the oldest of her line and the last ruler who saw the fleet built and sent. She holds a boundary petition to its ordinary end that same morning before going to her rooms and not rising again.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-III-0035"><em>Death of Queen Beathag</em>, 28 an t-Iuchar, LE 55</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-2526"></a>**17 an t-Samhain, LE 55** — *Raghnall mac Uilleim crowned at seven-and-forty* (Cathair dhearg). Raghnall mac Uilleim, son of Beathag and of Uilleam mac Iain, is crowned in An Talla Dearg within the month of his mother's death, seven-and-forty years old and long seated at her board. He wears a strip of undyed wool beneath his crowning colours, a thing he grew up watching his mother wear and never asked leave to wear himself.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0035"><em>Death of Queen Beathag</em>, 28 an t-Iuchar, LE 55</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-2527"></a>**12 an Dùbhlachd, LE 55** — *The empty place laid once more at the queen's wake* (Cathair dhearg). At the second night of Beathag's wake her steward lays the cup, trencher and straight knife once more at the foot of her table exactly as she always kept them, so that the court, passing between the small emptiness at the board's foot and the greater one at the board's head, cannot say with certainty whether the place is laid for the queen or still for the sister she mourned fifteen years across an unanswering sea.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0035"><em>Death of Queen Beathag</em>, 28 an t-Iuchar, LE 55</a>; ⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-III-0032"><em>The white sorrow first kept at court</em>, 27 an Dàmhair, LE 54</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-2528"></a>**18 an t-Samhain, LE 57** — *Murchadh mac Raghnaill takes the berths* (Seann Skell). The harbour-master of Seann Skell retires to his daughter's house up the Abhainn naomh rather than die at his post, and Murchadh mac Raghnaill, of an age with Niall mac Dhòmhnaill, takes the berths and the dues.
- <a id="ev-EIV-2529"></a>**7 an Lùnastal, LE 58** — *Death of Calum mac Nèill, Niall takes the harbour-house* (Seann Skell). Calum mac Nèill, harbour scribe of Seann Skell for six-and-fifty years, dies in the room above the harbour-house. The boards pass, as he had let the town see coming, to his grandson Niall mac Dhòmhnaill, the boy who once counted the hulls with a hazel stick, now a man of nine-and-twenty.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-III-0024"><em>The sunwise turn</em>, 19 an Giblean, LE 40</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-2530"></a>**5 an t-Sultain, LE 58** — *Dòmhnall mac Chaluim keeps the trade rolls* (Seann Skell). Passed over for the boards he had expected, Calum's son Dòmhnall keeps the harbour-house's trade rolls and dues, working the office beside his own son Niall without open quarrel, though he calls the boards the queerest inheritance a man could be passed over for.
- <a id="ev-EIV-2531"></a>**20 an Dàmhair, LE 58** — *Niall keeps his grandfather's stick at his own elbow* (Seann Skell). Niall takes down the hazel stick Calum kept since the night of An Diosal and sets it at his own writing-place rather than returning it to the shelf, though he puts it to no further use.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-III-0024"><em>The sunwise turn</em>, 19 an Giblean, LE 40</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0036"></a>**25 an t-Samhain, LE 61** — *The rite of the empty harbour*. A rite grows up about the quay the ships sailed from. It is still kept, lessened, on a day that none can now date truly.
- <a id="ev-EIV-2532"></a>**4 an Dàmhair, LE 62** — *The lamps kept on the rite's eve* (Seann Skell). On the eve nearest the day of An Diosal the households of Seann Skell bring small lights down to the west quay and set them along the stones the fleet sailed from, a rite grown up with no ordered beginning that Niall is the first to enter in the harbour-house's own leaves.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0036"><em>The rite of the empty harbour</em>, 25 an t-Samhain, LE 61</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0037"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, LE 64** — *The harbour at half trade* (Seann Skell). The harbour-master of Seann Skell finds his berths at half their old use, for the fishing households that crewed the fleet are gone. The rope-walks of Cuan shean turn off hands for the first time.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-2528"><em>Murchadh mac Raghnaill takes the berths</em>, 18 an t-Samhain, LE 57</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-2533"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, LE 64** — *The harbour-master's count of half trade* (Seann Skell). Murchadh mac Raghnaill, harbour-master of Seann Skell, sets his own reckoning of empty berths against full ones beside the boards: the harbour carries little more than half the trade it carried before An Diosal.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0037"><em>The harbour at half trade</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, LE 64</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-2534"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, LE 64** — *The rope-walks of Cuan shean let hands go* (Cuan shean). With more cordage made than the lessened harbour trade can use, the rope-walks along Cuan shean's waterfront turn off hands for the first time in the memory of any walker still living there.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0037"><em>The harbour at half trade</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, LE 64</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0038"></a>**8 an Gearran, LE 65** — *The second silence*. There is a rumour of a second, smaller crossing, with fewer ships and no word of where they went. Nothing that survives confirms or denies it.
- <a id="ev-EIV-2535"></a>**17 an t-Samhain, LE 65** — *Word of a second, smaller crossing* (Seann Skell). A hand off a coasting boat tells, at second or third remove, of a smaller fleet said to have sailed from the island's own shore in the years after An Diosal and never been heard from since. Niall hears the tale and, having no name or second mouth to stand behind it, sets it aside unwritten.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0038"><em>The second silence</em>, 8 an Gearran, LE 65</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-2536"></a>**28 am Faoilleach, LE 66** — *The first turn of Faire a' Chinn* (Ceann mhòr). Seonag nic Dhùghaill of Ceann mhòr climbs the headland at first light and keeps it through the day, seeing nothing but open water. Other households take up a turn of their own after her, and the custom becomes Faire a' Chinn.
- <a id="ev-EIV-2537"></a>**26 an Gearran, LE 66** — *The west quay's old name falls from use* (Seann Skell). The plain old name of the west quay falls out of common mouths at Seann Skell as carters, fish-wives and children too young to have known the fleet come to call it Cidhe an Diosail, without any single day anyone can name for the change.
- <a id="ev-III-0039"></a>**5 am Màrt, LE 67** — *The watch at Ceann mhòr* (Ceann mhòr). The fishing families of Ceann mhòr on the north-west coast keep a watch from the headland for returning sails, household by household in turn. The watch lapses within a generation. No sail is seen.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIV-2536"><em>The first turn of Faire a' Chinn</em>, 28 am Faoilleach, LE 66</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0040"></a>**13 am Màrt, LE 67** — *The west quay renamed*. The quay the ships sailed from is given a new name, so that common trade might go on under the old one without the memory. It is an early and quiet forgetting, made on purpose.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIV-2537"><em>The west quay's old name falls from use</em>, 26 an Gearran, LE 66</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0041"></a>**15 an Lùnastal, LE 67** — *Cidhe an Diosail* (Seann Skell). The departure berth is entered in the harbour rolls of Seann Skell as Cidhe an Diosail, the quay of the sunwise turn. The name Cidhe an Iar passes to the new fish-wharf at the north end of the strand, and within a few years the fishers use it without a thought.
- <a id="ev-III-0042"></a>**21 an Lùnastal, LE 67** — *Roghnaich takes its narrow sense*. In the custody-book the verb roghnaich, to choose, begins to stand with no object, meaning to have chosen the crossing. The scribes of the next century use it so without explaining it, the surest sign that it had passed into common speech.
- <a id="ev-III-0043"></a>**31 an Lùnastal, LE 67** — *The first generation that never saw the fleet*. Children born soon after the Setting-Out grow up never having seen the harbour with those ships in it. To them the leaving is already history.
- <a id="ev-EIV-2538"></a>**1 an t-Sultain, LE 67** — *Cidhe an Diosail entered in Rolla a' Chalaidh* (Seann Skell). Niall enters the west quay's new name into Rolla a' Chalaidh in his own hand, letting the old name stand once beside it, struck through but not scraped. The old name, Cidhe an Iar, passes to the new fish-wharf at the strand's north end.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0041"><em>Cidhe an Diosail</em>, 15 an Lùnastal, LE 67</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-2539"></a>**2 an t-Sultain, LE 67** — *Roghnaich stands with no object* (Seann Skell). In Rolla a' Chalaidh the word roghnaich, to choose, begins to stand alone in a clerk's hand, meaning to have chosen the crossing, and Niall lets the usage stand in his own leaves rather than write it out in full.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0042"><em>Roghnaich takes its narrow sense</em>, 21 an Lùnastal, LE 67</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-2540"></a>**3 an t-Sultain, LE 67** — *Niall's own children who never saw the fleet* (Seann Skell). Niall's eldest daughter, old enough by then to help about the harbour-house, asks whether he himself saw the ships go, having no memory of her own to set beside the wall of names she leans against.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0043"><em>The first generation that never saw the fleet</em>, 31 an Lùnastal, LE 67</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-2541"></a>**4 an t-Sultain, LE 67** — *Death of Alasdair Saor and his last coaster* (Seann Skell). Alasdair mac Iain, Alasdair Saor, who laid the fleet's first deep keel, dies at Seann Skell at the end of summer, days after launching a sewn-plank coaster at Inis àrsaidh for a fish merchant there, his last work. Niall enters the death and the quay's new name on the same leaf.
- <a id="ev-III-0044"></a>**8 an t-Sultain, LE 67** — *Death of Alasdair Saor* (Seann Skell). Alasdair Saor, who laid the first deep keel, dies at Seann Skell. His last work was a coasting trader of the old sewn-plank kind, built for a fish merchant of Inis àrsaidh.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIV-2541"><em>Death of Alasdair Saor and his last coaster</em>, 4 an t-Sultain, LE 67</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3001"></a>**14 an Dùbhlachd, LE 67** — *Coinneach mac Fhearghais named master of the fellowship* (Seann Skell). After Alasdair Saor's death Coinneach mac Fhearghais, the first apprentice Alasdair ever swore, takes the mastership of the fellowship of the strand, keeping its oath and its coal exactly as Alasdair had kept them before him.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0044"><em>Death of Alasdair Saor</em>, 8 an t-Sultain, LE 67</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3002"></a>**28 am Màrt, LE 68** — *Death of Coinneach mac Fhearghais* (Seann Skell). Coinneach mac Fhearghais dies at Seann Skell in the house where he had lived since his marriage, leaving the fellowship's coal to his eldest journeyman Griogair rather than to any man claiming it by right of years alone.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0044"><em>Death of Alasdair Saor</em>, 8 an t-Sultain, LE 67</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3003"></a>**27 an Gearran, LE 70** — *The one household that breaks its own coal* (Muileann dhearg). By the seventieth year of the count Eachann Briseadair's is the only household on the hill below Taigh na Fèithe that does the whole of the breaking and sorting itself rather than hiring hands season by season.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3004"></a>**29 am Faoilleach, LE 72** — *An Diosal count taken up at Cathair dhearg* (Cathair dhearg). The crown's own scribes at An Talla Dearg begin dating their rolls by the count Donnchadh mac Thormoid had kept alone at Taigh na Fèithe for near thirty years, setting aside the reckoning by a king's reign for the turning he first set his own hand to as a clerk of thirty.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3005"></a>**2 an Dùbhlachd, LE 72** — *Eachann Briseadair raises the first house below Taigh na Fèithe* (Muileann dhearg). Eachann Briseadair, whose household breaks and sorts the coal brought down from the galleries, builds the first house of stone below Taigh na Fèithe's own gate; his sons build three more beside it within the decade, the beginning of the coal-breakers' row.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3006"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, LE 72** — *Muileann dhearg a town in more than name* (Muileann dhearg). The coal-breakers' settlement below Taigh na Fèithe's gate, which has borne the name Muileann dhearg since the first years of the age, grows within Eachann Briseadair's lifetime into a town with its own well, smith and reeve, answering to Taigh na Fèithe rather than to any shire.
- <a id="ev-III-0045"></a>**27 an t-Ògmhios, LE 84** — *The shipwrights' fellowship ends*. No more sea-going ships being wanted, the fellowship that built the fleet of the Sundering quietly breaks up. Its craft is half forgotten by the time anyone needs it again.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIV-3003"><em>The one household that breaks its own coal</em>, 27 an Gearran, LE 70</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3007"></a>**25 an t-Sultain, LE 84** — *The fellowship of the strand released* (Seann Skell). Griogair calls the fellowship's remaining journeymen to the strand and releases every man from the oath, judging there is no longer craft enough in the island's own boat-building to keep it; the journeymen scatter to the rope-walks, their fathers' land and Doire fhionn's coppice-cutting.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0045"><em>The shipwrights' fellowship ends</em>, 27 an t-Ògmhios, LE 84</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0046"></a>**29 an Cèitean, LE 85** — *The keel-moulds burned* (Seann Skell). In a hard season the patterns and moulds of the broken fellowship, kept in a shed on the strand at Seann Skell, are burned for firewood. The harbour-master notes the loss of the shed and not of what was in it.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3008"></a>**21 an Dùbhlachd, LE 85** — *The keel-moulds burned for firewood* (Seann Skell). In the hard winter of Faolach the fellowship's old patterns and keel-moulds, untouched for years in the shed on the strand, are carried out and burned; the harbour-master notes only that the shed came down, and nothing of what it held.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0046"><em>The keel-moulds burned</em>, 29 an Cèitean, LE 85</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3009"></a>**6 an t-Sultain, LE 86** — *The lots drawn among Na Seachd Taighean* (Muileann dhearg). The heads of Na Seachd Taighean that hold the right to the coal are called to Taigh na Fèithe and each draws a marked stone from a covered bag before the custodians and the household, the galleries falling as the stones fall so that no house may claim its ground was given rather than drawn.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3010"></a>**9 an t-Ògmhios, LE 92** — *Death of Raghnall mac Uilleim and the crowning of his son* (Cathair dhearg). Raghnall mac Uilleim dies in his eighty-fifth year after seven-and-thirty years on An Talla Dearg; his son Raghnall mac Raghnaill, seven-and-forty years old, is crowned in his place without dispute, Leabhar a' Chùraim giving the closed reign one line and the new one another.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3011"></a>**8 an t-Iuchar, LE 92** — *Birth of Ìomhar mac Raghnaill* (Cathair dhearg). In the year his grandfather dies and his father is crowned, a son, Ìomhar, is born at Cathair dhearg to Raghnall mac Raghnaill, a king of seven-and-forty with a new crown and a new child in the same season.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3012"></a>**6 an Lùnastal, LE 100** — *Death of Eachann Briseadair* (Muileann dhearg). Eachann Briseadair dies at sixty in the shed where he broke his first load of coal as a boy, his sons and grandsons already keeping the work; he is buried on the rise above the row with a lump of unbroken coal set over him rather than a mason's stone.

## The Years LE 101 – 200

- <a id="ev-EIV-3013"></a>**4 an t-Sultain, LE 104** — *Death of Niall mac Dhòmhnaill* (Seann Skell). Niall mac Dhòmhnaill dies at Seann Skell in the harbour-house itself, six-and-forty years after taking up the boards, his grandfather's notched hazel stick set in his hand at his own asking and buried with him, the count it held never once spoken aloud.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-III-0024"><em>The sunwise turn</em>, 19 an Giblean, LE 40</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0047"></a>**30 an Giblean, LE 109** — *The mountain divided among the houses* (Muileann dhearg). The seven houses draw lots at the vein-house for the galleries each will keep, and the vein-house confirms each its Small-Burning measure. The lot-stones were kept in a bag at Muileann dhearg and shown to visitors for centuries after.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIV-3009"><em>The lots drawn among Na Seachd Taighean</em>, 6 an t-Sultain, LE 86</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0048"></a>**14 an t-Iuchar, LE 109** — *The coppice law of Doire fhionn* (Doire fhionn). The great oaks gone to the fleet, the shire of Doire fhionn forbids the felling of any living oak without the reeve's mark and begins to cut its woods by coppice. The law spreads to every shire with a Doire in its name.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-1510"><em>The Child walled</em>, 19 an Dùbhlachd, LE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0049"></a>**12 an Lùnastal, LE 109** — *The lamps kept at Seann Skell* (Seann Skell). The waterfront of Seann Skell keeps the night of lamps each year on the eve of the rite of the empty harbour. The children are told the lamps are for ships coming home, and the priests do not gainsay it.
- <a id="ev-III-0050"></a>**9 an Dàmhair, LE 109** — *Death of Donnchadh mac Thormoid* (Muileann dhearg). Donnchadh mac Thormoid, the vein-house scribe who began the count of years, dies at Muileann dhearg. His last entry is the season's burning of coal, household by household, in the same hand as his first.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3014"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, LE 109** — *Clachan a' Chrannchuir shown to a visitor* (Muileann dhearg). Old Donnchadh takes the bag of Clachan a' Chrannchuir down from its peg to let a grandson of Eachann Briseadair's, waiting idle in Taigh na Fèithe hall, hold it and hear how the seven heads once drew their galleries, though he tells the boy nothing of which stone fell to which house.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0047"><em>The mountain divided among the houses</em>, 30 an Giblean, LE 109</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3015"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, LE 109** — *Death of Donnchadh mac Thormoid* (Muileann dhearg). Donnchadh mac Thormoid dies at Muileann dhearg in his ninety-fifth year, his last entry the season's burning of coal household by household, set down in the same careful hand he had used since he was fifteen.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0050"><em>Death of Donnchadh mac Thormoid</em>, 9 an Dàmhair, LE 109</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0051"></a>**7 an t-Samhain, LE 125** — *Raghnall dies; Ìomhar crowned* (Cathair dhearg). King Raghnall mac Raghnaill dies at Cathair dhearg, and his son Ìomhar mac Raghnaill is crowned. Raghnall had followed his father Raghnall mac Uilleim, who died in his eighty-fifth year after a long and quiet reign; the custody-book gives each of the two Raghnalls a single line.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EIV-2508"><em>Birth of Raghnall mac Raghnaill</em>, 6 an Lùnastal, LE 45</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EIV-3011"><em>Birth of Ìomhar mac Raghnaill</em>, 8 an t-Iuchar, LE 92</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3016"></a>**22 an t-Samhain, LE 125** — *The old men compare two crownings* (Cathair dhearg). At Cathair dhearg the court remarks that Ìomhar mac Raghnaill's crowning differs little from his father's three-and-thirty years before, the same cup passed hand to hand and the same oath said over it, a quiet continuity Leabhar a' Chùraim itself gives only a single line apiece.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0051"><em>Raghnall dies; Ìomhar crowned</em>, 7 an t-Samhain, LE 125</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3017"></a>**11 an Cèitean, LE 130** — *A boy of Inis mhòr asks why the barges keep the coast* (Inis mhòr). Watching the first grain barge loaded on the Abhainn ghorm, a boy of Inis mhòr asks his father why the boat should not simply cross open water by the shorter way, and is answered only with a look and no word, for no one on the island since the fleet has wished to be out of sight of land.
- <a id="ev-III-0052"></a>**6 an Dùbhlachd, LE 149** — *The silversmiths of Muileann chiar* (Muileann chiar — baile mèinne airgid). Silver of the seam at Muileann chiar, mined since the Holy Age, is wrought into neck-rings for the heads of the seven houses. The smiths' fellowship of the seam, heirs of Sliochd Fhearchair, keeps its craft within four families.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3018"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, LE 149** — *The first silver neck-rings worn* (Muileann chiar — baile mèinne airgid). The heads of Na Seachd Taighean first wear the neck-rings beaten by the smiths of Muileann chiar, so that a stranger at Taigh na Fèithe or An Talla Dearg may know a custodian by the collar at his throat before a word is said.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0052"><em>The silversmiths of Muileann chiar</em>, 6 an Dùbhlachd, LE 149</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0053"></a>**4 am Faoilleach, LE 154** — *Inis mhòr's grain fleet* (Inis mhòr). Inis mhòr in the north builds barges to carry grain down the Abhainn ghorm to Caol bheag, and from Ros chiar at the river mouth west along the coast to Cnoc bheag. They are sewn-plank boats of the old kind, and none lies a night out of sight of land.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIV-3017"><em>A boy of Inis mhòr asks why the barges keep the coast</em>, 11 an Cèitean, LE 130</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0054"></a>**2 an Gearran, LE 156** — *The coughing sickness at Caol fhiadhaich* (Caol fhiadhaich). A coughing sickness runs through Caol fhiadhaich on the south-west coast and kills some ten before it burns out. The shared meal is kept throughout, and the reeve holds that it saved the rest.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3019"></a>**27 an Giblean, LE 156** — *The shared meal kept through the cough* (Caol fhiadhaich). When the coughing sickness reaches the reeve's own household at Caol fhiadhaich, his wife refuses to let their door be barred against the shared board, holding that a household which eats apart out of fear will go on eating apart after the fear has passed; she lives, and the custom outlasts the sickness.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0054"><em>The coughing sickness at Caol fhiadhaich</em>, 2 an Gearran, LE 156</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3020"></a>**22 an Dàmhair, LE 157** — *Birth of Fearchar mac Lachlainn* (Baile Mòr dhomhain). A son, Fearchar, is born in the house of Clann Fhearchair at Baile Mòr dhomhain, the elder of two brothers, in a hall that has never looked for a crown and does not look for one now.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3021"></a>**23 an t-Sultain, LE 160** — *The king's habit at the gallery's mouth* (Muileann dhearg). King Ìomhar takes up a habit no ruler before him is recorded keeping, asking the youngest hand at any gallery he visits to name the prop, the cut and the tally-mark before him; Taigh na Fèithe's scribe judges it a kind of counting of his own, made by a king with no child to leave the hall to.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-III-0051"><em>Raghnall dies; Ìomhar crowned</em>, 7 an t-Samhain, LE 125</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3022"></a>**30 an t-Sultain, LE 163** — *A singing timber clears the gallery* (Muileann dhearg). Bound as a child to a custodian's household, Fearchar mac Lachlainn stands outside a mountain gallery in the night while the custodian, hearing a timber begin to sing, has the working cleared an hour before the prop gives way with no one beneath it; he keeps the memory into his own old age.
- <a id="ev-III-0055"></a>**3 am Màrt, LE 164** — *Am Buabhall Fortanach rebuilt in stone* (Am Buabhall Fortanach). The old road-house of Am Buabhall Fortanach burns to its footings, and its keeper, Eilidh nic Chaluim, rebuilds it in stone. It is already known for its jugged buffalo.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3023"></a>**1 an Giblean, LE 164** — *Am Buabhall Fortanach's new stone walls* (Am Buabhall Fortanach). Eilidh nic Chaluim raises the burned road-house of Am Buabhall Fortanach again in stone, and a boy of Clann Fhearchair riding out with his father to see the walls going up is given a bowl of the jugged buffalo before the roof itself is finished.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0055"><em>Am Buabhall Fortanach rebuilt in stone</em>, 3 am Màrt, LE 164</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3024"></a>**30 an t-Sultain, LE 164** — *Fearchar mac Lachlainn bound to the galleries* (Muileann dhearg). At seven years old Fearchar mac Lachlainn is bound for seven years to a custodian's household above Muileann dhearg, as every child of Na Seachd Taighean is meant to be, while his younger brother Iain is kept at home to learn the hall.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3025"></a>**30 an Cèitean, LE 170** — *Death of Raghnall Beag mac Ìomhair* (Cathair dhearg). King Ìomhar's only son, Raghnall Beag, dies of a fever at Cathair dhearg; a custodian of Clann Fhearchair reads the letter aloud and says that a king with no other child is a house with one wall standing, which the wind will find sooner or later.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3026"></a>**16 an Dàmhair, LE 171** — *Fearchar comes home from the galleries* (Baile Mòr dhomhain). Fearchar mac Lachlainn comes home to Baile Mòr dhomhain at fourteen, able to tell the weight of a sealed measure by its heft and the sound a gallery makes when its timbering has begun to fail.
- <a id="ev-III-0056"></a>**7 an Dàmhair, LE 179** — *The spirit-house at Dùn ìseal* (Dùn ìseal). The keepers of the Old Spirits, the faith of the hearths, raise a house for the ancestors at Dùn ìseal, and cut the names of the dead of the eastern shires on wooden posts. The posts are cut anew each generation as the old ones rot.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3027"></a>**30 an Dàmhair, LE 179** — *Names cut new on the posts of Dùn ìseal* (Dùn ìseal). A young man of Clann Fhearchair, travelling east with his father, stands long before the wooden posts of the spirit-house at Dùn ìseal, reading names the shire itself cuts anew each generation, and says only that a shire which trusts wood to hold its dead must trust its own memory further than he would.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0056"><em>The spirit-house at Dùn ìseal</em>, 7 an Dàmhair, LE 179</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3028"></a>**23 an t-Samhain, LE 179** — *The head of Clann Fhearchair names his younger son* (Baile Mòr dhomhain). The head of Clann Fhearchair dies at Baile Mòr dhomhain, naming his younger son Iain mac Lachlainn to the headship of the house and leaving his elder son Fearchar to the galleries he knows.
- <a id="ev-III-0057"></a>**30 an Giblean, LE 180** — *Ìomhar dies without an heir* (Cathair dhearg). King Ìomhar mac Raghnaill dies at Cathair dhearg with no living child, and with him ends the line of Beathag. The heads of the seven houses are summoned to the capital to name a king.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-3025"><em>Death of Raghnall Beag mac Ìomhair</em>, 30 an Cèitean, LE 170</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3029"></a>**13 an Cèitean, LE 181** — *The heads of the seven summoned to the capital* (Cathair dhearg). With King Ìomhar dead and no living child of his line, riders carry word to all of Na Seachd Taighean that their heads are summoned to Cathair dhearg to choose, for the first time since An Diosal, a king the crown's own blood cannot simply hand down.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0057"><em>Ìomhar dies without an heir</em>, 30 an Giblean, LE 180</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0058"></a>**19 an Gearran, LE 182** — *Fearchar mac Lachlainn chosen* (Cathair dhearg). The heads of the houses choose Fearchar mac Lachlainn of Baile Mòr dhomhain, of Clann Fhearchair, and he is crowned at Cathair dhearg. He is the first king made by the seven houses and not by descent.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EIV-3020"><em>Birth of Fearchar mac Lachlainn</em>, 22 an Dàmhair, LE 157</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-3024"><em>Fearchar mac Lachlainn bound to the galleries</em>, 30 an t-Sultain, LE 164</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-3026"><em>Fearchar comes home from the galleries</em>, 16 an Dàmhair, LE 171</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-3028"><em>The head of Clann Fhearchair names his younger son</em>, 23 an t-Samhain, LE 179</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-3029"><em>The heads of the seven summoned to the capital</em>, 13 an Cèitean, LE 181</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3030"></a>**21 an Giblean, LE 182** — *Iain mac Lachlainn turns the choosing aside* (Cathair dhearg). Named by the other heads as a possible king, Iain mac Lachlainn of Clann Fhearchair turns the honour aside, saying a man who keeps one house's hall well may yet keep a kingdom poorly, and names his elder brother Fearchar in his place.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-III-0058"><em>Fearchar mac Lachlainn chosen</em>, 19 an Gearran, LE 182</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3031"></a>**19 an t-Iuchar, LE 182** — *A borrowed cup for the first oath* (Cathair dhearg). With no cup of the crown's own ready for the rite, the head of Clann Mhuirich sends for the cup her own house keeps, so that Fearchar mac Lachlainn drinks his first oath as king from a vessel that belongs, strictly, to one house among the seven rather than to the crown.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0058"><em>Fearchar mac Lachlainn chosen</em>, 19 an Gearran, LE 182</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3032"></a>**5 an t-Sultain, LE 182** — *The head of Clann Ìomhair breaks the silence in the yard* (Cathair dhearg). After a morning's silence in the yard of An Talla Dearg the head of Clann Ìomhair speaks first: the line of Beathag has held the hall a hundred years and more, and no house of the seven has a better claim to it than another.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-III-0058"><em>Fearchar mac Lachlainn chosen</em>, 19 an Gearran, LE 182</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3033"></a>**2 an Giblean, LE 188** — *Birth of Fearchar Donn* (Cathair dhearg). A son is born to King Fearchar mac Lachlainn, then one-and-thirty and six years crowned, and is called Fearchar Donn for the brown of his hair; he is the first child born to a king Na Seachd Taighean chose.
- <a id="ev-III-0059"></a>**20 am Màrt, LE 194** — *A court at Baile Mòr dhomhain* (Baile Mòr dhomhain). King Fearchar keeps his court part of each year at Baile Mòr dhomhain, near the mountain, that he may take counsel of the vein-house without a journey. The double court lasts as long as his house.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3034"></a>**10 an Dùbhlachd, LE 194** — *The double court divided* (Baile Mòr dhomhain). King Fearchar settles the custom of keeping his court partly at Cathair dhearg and partly at Baile Mòr dhomhain near Taigh na Fèithe, with his brother Iain keeping Clann Fhearchair's own hall whenever the court is away at the capital.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0059"><em>A court at Baile Mòr dhomhain</em>, 20 am Màrt, LE 194</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3035"></a>**19 an Cèitean, LE 195** — *Fearchar Donn asked the child's question* (Muileann dhearg). Brought young to the mountain as his father had been, Fearchar Donn is asked at seven years old to name the prop, the cut and the tally-mark before him at a gallery's mouth, and gives an answer his father calls, laughing, the first honestly ordinary thing his own house has produced in two reigns.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3036"></a>**28 an t-Ògmhios, LE 200** — *The brothers' leaf-book of letters* (Baile Mòr dhomhain). A later hand at Baile Mòr dhomhain gathers into one leaf-book the letters King Fearchar and his brother Iain exchange across every season of the divided court, boundary disputes and grain petitions set down beside a long-running complaint over the capital's cooking.

## The Years LE 201 – 300

- <a id="ev-III-0060"></a>**21 an Gearran, LE 209** — *The fishers of Àth fhiadhaich* (Àth fhiadhaich). After a season of losses the fishing families of Àth fhiadhaich join in one fellowship to share boats and nets. It is the first fishers' fellowship on the east coast.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3037"></a>**27 an t-Iuchar, LE 210** — *A fisherman questioned on the fellowship* (Àth fhiadhaich). Brought before the old king almost by chance, a fisherman of Àth fhiadhaich is kept a full hour answering questions on how boats and nets are shared among the new fellowship's households, and rides home understanding only afterward that the king was asking after the fellowship itself, not the fish.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0060"><em>The fishers of Àth fhiadhaich</em>, 21 an Gearran, LE 209</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0061"></a>**21 an t-Ògmhios, LE 211** — *Fearchar Donn crowned* (Cathair dhearg). Fearchar mac Lachlainn dies, and his son, called Fearchar Donn, is crowned at Cathair dhearg without dispute.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EIV-3033"><em>Birth of Fearchar Donn</em>, 2 an Giblean, LE 188</a>; ⇝ Legacy of <a href="#ev-EIV-3035"><em>Fearchar Donn asked the child's question</em>, 19 an Cèitean, LE 195</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3038"></a>**10 an t-Sultain, LE 211** — *A king's fire kept to the ordinary measure* (Baile Mòr dhomhain). Dying, King Fearchar asks that no coal be burned beyond the ordinary handful for any rite made over him, and Taigh na Fèithe keeps the asking to the letter, so that the fire lit for a king is no larger than the fire any house of the seven lights for its own dead.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0061"><em>Fearchar Donn crowned</em>, 21 an t-Ògmhios, LE 211</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3039"></a>**13 an t-Samhain, LE 211** — *Na Seachd Taighean stand at Clann Fhearchair's grave* (Baile Mòr dhomhain). The heads of Na Seachd Taighean, each still wearing the neck-ring of Muileann chiar, stand at the grave of the king they chose nine-and-twenty years before, and not one of them is heard to say the choosing made in that cold yard was anything other than the right one.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-III-0061"><em>Fearchar Donn crowned</em>, 21 an t-Ògmhios, LE 211</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3040"></a>**21 an Gearran, LE 215** — *A hawk overfed will not come to the glove* (Cnoc bheag). A young bird of the mews at Cnoc bheag, fed too heavy the evening before, will not answer Gormshuil nic Artair's call at the dawn rite; her father Artair, too stiff now to climb to the block himself, tells her plainly that a bird fed past its measure is as useless as one starved of it.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3041"></a>**5 an Dùbhlachd, LE 218** — *Gormshuil calls Mòd down alone for the first time* (Cnoc bheag). With Artair's knees failed for the climb, Gormshuil nic Artair goes up to the mews block at Cnoc bheag before dawn and calls the shrine's hawk down with no one else to answer for the flight, three-and-thirty years old and, by her own later word, more frightened coming down than going up.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3042"></a>**6 an t-Samhain, LE 220** — *Death of Artair, hawk-keeper of Cnoc bheag* (Cnoc bheag). Artair dies at Cnoc bheag in his own bed above the shrine, three-score and ten years old, and the keeping of the mews he had held the better part of his life passes without dispute to his daughter Gormshuil; the hill's households bury him facing the shrine rather than in any rite of the departed.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3043"></a>**8 an Dàmhair, LE 221** — *Gormshuil first names the vein An Seabhag Acrach* (Cnoc bheag). Asked, as custom wants, to say a few words over her father's empty place on the bench, Gormshuil nic Artair tells the shrine's watchers for the first time that the vein under Muileann dhearg is itself a hawk of Mòd's kind, to be fed the measured handful and never glutted past it.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3044"></a>**31 am Màrt, LE 225** — *Hawk-keepers of the north coast come to hear her* (Cnoc bheag). Word of Gormshuil's teaching, carried inland by a wool-buyer of Bàgh an t-Seabhaig, brings three keepers of the coastal shrines to Cnoc bheag to judge it for themselves; they stay a week among the coal-cutters' wives at the shrine's ledge and go home saying the teaching has lost nothing in the carrying.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3045"></a>**29 an Giblean, LE 225** — *Bàgh an t-Seabhaig elder questions Gormshuil's own hunger* (Cnoc bheag). The eldest of the three coastal keepers asks Gormshuil, on the last morning of their visit, whether she has ever gone hungry enough herself to know the second half of what she teaches; Gormshuil answers that she has, twice, and disliked the lesson both times without forgetting either.
- <a id="ev-III-0062"></a>**20 an Giblean, LE 229** — *Gormshuil of the Hawk* (Cnoc bheag). At Cnoc bheag, where the dawn-hawk rite of the Holy Age is still kept, the priestess Gormshuil nic Artair teaches that the hawk of the rite is Mòd, the Hawk of Acaill, as old as Fionntan mac Bòchra, eldest of men, and remembering all things with him. The vein, she teaches, is the Hungry Hawk, to be fed the measured handful and no more, for a hawk overfed will not hunt and a hawk starved will turn on the hand. Her followers gather the old rite into the first house of Òrd an t-Seabhaig, the order of the Hawk of Acaill.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-3040"><em>A hawk overfed will not come to the glove</em>, 21 an Gearran, LE 215</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-3041"><em>Gormshuil calls Mòd down alone for the first time</em>, 5 an Dùbhlachd, LE 218</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-3042"><em>Death of Artair, hawk-keeper of Cnoc bheag</em>, 6 an t-Samhain, LE 220</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIV-3043"><em>Gormshuil first names the vein An Seabhag Acrach</em>, 8 an Dàmhair, LE 221</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIV-3044"><em>Hawk-keepers of the north coast come to hear her</em>, 31 am Màrt, LE 225</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIV-3045"><em>Bàgh an t-Seabhaig elder questions Gormshuil's own hunger</em>, 29 an Giblean, LE 225</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3046"></a>**31 an Cèitean, LE 229** — *Gormshuil's first true congregation* (Cnoc bheag). The watchers climbing to Cnoc bheag for the dawn rite grow past the number the shrine's ledge can easily hold, and Gormshuil, asked more mornings than not to give the teaching whole, gathers it at last into the shape it will keep for the rest of her life.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0062"><em>Gormshuil of the Hawk</em>, 20 an Giblean, LE 229</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3047"></a>**1 an Gearran, LE 232** — *Taigh an t-Seabhaig raised* (Cnoc bheag). Gormshuil's watchers, calling themselves a house rather than a congregation, raise a hall of timber and dry stone below the mews block at Cnoc bheag, giving the old dawn-hawk rite a roof of its own for the first time in its keeping.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0062"><em>Gormshuil of the Hawk</em>, 20 an Giblean, LE 229</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0063"></a>**22 am Màrt, LE 239** — *The hawk-house at Ros gheal* (Ros gheal). Gormshuil's pupils found a second house of the Hawk at Ros gheal. Its priests take charge of the measured burning for all the country between Ros gheal on the coast and Cnoc bheag up the river.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3048"></a>**27 an Lùnastal, LE 239** — *A second house raised at Ros gheal* (Ros gheal). Two of Gormshuil's pupils, a brother and sister of a coastal household, carry the dawn rite down to the shore at Ros gheal rather than make every fisher's family of that coast walk two days inland; Gormshuil goes down herself to judge the teaching had travelled whole.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-III-0063"><em>The hawk-house at Ros gheal</em>, 22 am Màrt, LE 239</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3049"></a>**25 an t-Iuchar, LE 243** — *Birth of Sìleas nic Fhearchair* (Cathair dhearg). A daughter, Sìleas, is born at Cathair dhearg to King Fearchar Donn in the two-and-thirtieth year of his reign, when he is five-and-fifty years old; she is his only child to live.
- <a id="ev-III-0064"></a>**17 an t-Ògmhios, LE 244** — *Flood at Seann Vell* (Seann Vell). In a wet spring the river at Seann Vell on the south-east coast breaks its banks and carries away the lower mills. The mill-wrights build them again on the higher bank.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3050"></a>**8 an Dùbhlachd, LE 244** — *A pupil reports the flood at Seann Vell* (Seann Vell). A pupil of the Ros gheal house, present on other business when the river at Seann Vell breaks its banks and carries away the lower mills, calls the flood a kind of overfed hawk; Gormshuil tells him plainly that a river is a river and not a hawk, and sends him back to watch the mills rebuilt before he judges further.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0064"><em>Flood at Seann Vell</em>, 17 an t-Ògmhios, LE 244</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3051"></a>**12 am Màrt, LE 247** — *Death of Gormshuil nic Artair* (Cnoc bheag). Gormshuil dies at Cnoc bheag, two-and-sixty years old, in the season the house at Ros gheal marks its own eighth year, and is buried, at her own asking, on the open hillside beside her father rather than within the hall her own teaching raised.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3052"></a>**3 an t-Ògmhios, LE 251** — *Ùisdean mac Pàdraig marks the sayings he did not hear* (Cnoc bheag). Gathering Gormshuil's teaching into a single book, Ùisdean mac Pàdraig travels as far as Ros gheal to set down what her pupils remember, marking plainly every saying he did not hear from her own mouth; when the book is finished the marked sayings far outnumber the rest.
- <a id="ev-III-0065"></a>**5 an t-Ògmhios, LE 251** — *The sayings of Gormshuil written* (Cnoc bheag). After Gormshuil's death her sayings are written at Cnoc bheag as Leabhar an t-Seabhaig, the Book of the Hawk. The copyist, Ùisdean mac Pàdraig, marks every saying he did not hear from her own mouth, and these are the greater part.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-3051"><em>Death of Gormshuil nic Artair</em>, 12 am Màrt, LE 247</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIV-3052"><em>Ùisdean mac Pàdraig marks the sayings he did not hear</em>, 3 an t-Ògmhios, LE 251</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3501"></a>**21 an Dàmhair, LE 256** — *The death of King Fearchar Donn* (Cathair dhearg). Fearchar Donn dies at Cathair dhearg in his sixty-eighth year, the last of his own riding to Taigh na Fèithe's winter burning long past. His daughter Sìleas, thirteen years old, is judged too young to be crowned, and the heads of the seven custodian houses take the hall in her name by turns.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3502"></a>**26 an t-Iuchar, LE 258** — *Sìleas nic Fhearchair crowned* (Cathair dhearg). Sìleas, fifteen years old, is crowned at Cathair dhearg with the same cup and the same oath as her father before her. The heads of Na Seachd Taighean swear over her hands to hold the vein and its right as it has always been held.
- <a id="ev-III-0066"></a>**23 an t-Samhain, LE 259** — *The storm that took Seann Toll's boats* (Seann Toll). A northern storm, named Am Fuath Mòr in the harbour rolls, breaks the harbour wall of Seann Toll and sinks forty boats at their moorings. Eighteen fishers drown.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3503"></a>**11 an Dùbhlachd, LE 259** — *Raghnall mac Nèill in the water at Seann Toll* (Seann Toll). In the storm the north coast calls Am Fuath Mòr, Raghnall mac Nèill, reeve of Seann Toll, thirty-four years old and four years in office, stands knee-deep on the strand hauling on a rope with three other men to bring in a boat with two children lashed inside it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0066"><em>The storm that took Seann Toll's boats</em>, 23 an t-Samhain, LE 259</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3504"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, LE 259** — *The dead of Am Fuath Mòr buried on the headland* (Seann Toll). Seann Toll buries the eighteen who drowned trying to save the boats in a single row on the headland above the broken wall, a row so long that the reeve keeping the count loses his place twice and begins again.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0066"><em>The storm that took Seann Toll's boats</em>, 23 an t-Samhain, LE 259</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3505"></a>**14 an Gearran, LE 260** — *The queen weds Dùghall mac Ìomhair* (Cathair dhearg). Sìleas takes a consort of her own choosing, Dùghall mac Ìomhair of the eastern hill-house Clann Ìomhair, whom she has known since the years of her regency. Na Seachd Taighean' heads attend the wedding at Cathair dhearg.
- <a id="ev-III-0067"></a>**16 an t-Iuchar, LE 261** — *Seann Toll walls its harbour again* (Seann Toll). Seann Toll builds its harbour wall again, higher and with a hooked end, to a plan the reeve had from the masons of the capital. The wall stands through every storm of this age.
- <a id="ev-III-0068"></a>**12 an t-Sultain, LE 261** — *The walls of Dùn dhearg* (Dùn dhearg). Clann Ìomhair, who hold the land about Dùn dhearg in the eastern hills, wall it in stone. These are the first walls on the island raised by a custodian house and not by the crown.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-3505"><em>The queen weds Dùghall mac Ìomhair</em>, 14 an Gearran, LE 260</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0069"></a>**11 an Dàmhair, LE 261** — *Queen Sìleas's measures* (Cathair dhearg). Sìleas nic Fhearchair, crowned after her father Fearchar Donn, fixes one measure for grain across the island, the firlot of Cathair dhearg, so that barter between shires need not begin with a quarrel over the size of a basket. Firlots of oak bound with iron are sent to every shire seat.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EIV-3049"><em>Birth of Sìleas nic Fhearchair</em>, 25 an t-Iuchar, LE 243</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-3501"><em>The death of King Fearchar Donn</em>, 21 an Dàmhair, LE 256</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-3502"><em>Sìleas nic Fhearchair crowned</em>, 26 an t-Iuchar, LE 258</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3506"></a>**25 an Dàmhair, LE 261** — *A cold supper at An Talla Dearg* (Dùn dhearg). Sìleas summons the head of Clann Ìomhair to a supper at Cathair dhearg after his house walls Dùn dhearg without the crown's leave. Neither speaks plainly of the walls; both understand what is meant by everything left unsaid, and the walls stand unopposed.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0068"><em>The walls of Dùn dhearg</em>, 12 an t-Sultain, LE 261</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3507"></a>**2 an t-Samhain, LE 261** — *The quarrel over a basket at the capital's market* (Cathair dhearg). Watching a farmer and a grain-seller come near to blows below An Talla Dearg over the true size of a basket, Sìleas is put in mind of a like quarrel she watched as a child, and resolves that one measure alone shall serve the whole island.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-III-0069"><em>Queen Sìleas's measures</em>, 11 an Dàmhair, LE 261</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3508"></a>**12 an Cèitean, LE 262** — *The firlots carried to the shire seats* (Cathair dhearg). Oak firlots bound with three iron hoops, each cut to the capital's standard and marked with the queen's own mark, go out by cart from Cathair dhearg to every shire seat on the island, so that a basket weighed true at the capital weighs true anywhere a Dia-thìrich stands to sell or buy.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0069"><em>Queen Sìleas's measures</em>, 11 an Dàmhair, LE 261</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3509"></a>**15 am Màrt, LE 270** — *The first quarrel settled by the firlot* (Àth shean). At Àth shean a carter and a miller who have fallen out over a load of oats are measured true against the town's firlot before a crowd their shouting drew, and the matter is settled before either of them thinks to shout further.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0069"><em>Queen Sìleas's measures</em>, 11 an Dàmhair, LE 261</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3510"></a>**10 an t-Ògmhios, LE 270** — *Birth of Uisdean mac Dhùghaill* (Cathair dhearg). Sìleas and Dùghall's son Uisdean is born at Cathair dhearg, a quiet and watchful child who is one day to follow his mother in the hall.
- <a id="ev-III-0070"></a>**22 an t-Sultain, LE 284** — *Tally-houses in the royal granaries* (Cathair dhearg). Queen Sìleas sets a tally-house in each royal granary, where every exchange of grain for cloth, salt or labour is cut on paired sticks, one for each party. It is the first reckoning of trade across the whole island, and it runs without coin.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3511"></a>**17 an Dàmhair, LE 284** — *A trader questions the tally-stick at Cathair dhearg* (Cathair dhearg). At the granary tally-house a trader of the long city asks the clerk what stops a false notch being cut after a bargain is struck, and is shown how the grain of a split stick runs true only when its two halves are laid together again.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0070"><em>Tally-houses in the royal granaries</em>, 22 an t-Sultain, LE 284</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0070a"></a>**17 an t-Samhain, LE 287** — *The market charter of Cathair fhada* (Cathair fhada). Queen Sìleas grants Cathair fhada a market on its ridge at every full moon, with a tally-house for the south; it is the first market right cut on paired sticks. The merchants of the long city carry the honey, hemp, wax and pots of the south to the capital, and begin to go as one company to the harvest fair at Muileann òg.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3512"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, LE 287** — *The first full-moon market at Cathair fhada* (Cathair fhada). Under the new charter the long city holds its first market timed to the full moon, and traders come from three days' walk in every direction to carry honey, hemp, wax and pottery north as one company.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0070a"><em>The market charter of Cathair fhada</em>, 17 an t-Samhain, LE 287</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0071"></a>**21 an Dàmhair, LE 289** — *Drochaid Cathair dhearg widened* (Drochaid Cathair dhearg). The old stone bridge over Abhainn dhomhain at Cathair dhearg is widened for two carts to pass. Queen Sìleas's name is cut on the downstream parapet, and may still be read there.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3513"></a>**8 an t-Samhain, LE 289** — *The bridge of Cathair dhearg widened* (Drochaid Cathair dhearg). The old stone bridge over Abhainn dhomhain at Cathair dhearg is widened for two loaded carts to pass abreast, and the queen's name is cut into the downstream parapet without her asking for it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0071"><em>Drochaid Cathair dhearg widened</em>, 21 an Dàmhair, LE 289</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3514"></a>**11 an Dùbhlachd, LE 289** — *Sìleas rides to the widened bridge with her son* (Cathair dhearg). On a grey morning in Bearnach Queen Sìleas rides down to see Drochaid Cathair dhearg finished, widened for two carts abreast, forty-six years old, with her son Uisdean, nineteen, riding at her side.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0071"><em>Drochaid Cathair dhearg widened</em>, 21 an Dàmhair, LE 289</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3515"></a>**21 an Dàmhair, LE 300** — *Coinneach mac Mhàrtainn on the carters' roads*. Coinneach mac Mhàrtainn, a druid of the schools of Flidais who has walked the roads of the middle shires for the better part of forty years, carries the stag's teaching from house to house with a stick, a satchel of writing-boards and no fixed hearth.

## The Years LE 301 – 400

- <a id="ev-III-0072"></a>**26 an t-Iuchar, LE 304** — *The crossing days of the panthers* (Imrich nam Pantar). In the southern hills near Imrich nam Pantar the herders keep the panther roads clear on the days the great cats cross, and drive their flocks off the paths beforehand. The crossing days are the first thing the southern shires agree on in writing.
- <a id="ev-III-0073"></a>**24 an Lùnastal, LE 304** — *An Leòmhann Buidhe on the north road* (An Leòmhann Buidhe). An Leòmhann Buidhe, a road-house on the northern mining road, serves the coal-carters oatcakes fried in linseed oil, and fire water. Its keeper is fined for watering the fire water.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-3515"><em>Coinneach mac Mhàrtainn on the carters' roads</em>, 21 an Dàmhair, LE 300</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3516"></a>**20 an t-Sultain, LE 304** — *Coinneach among the panther-herders* (Imrich nam Pantar). Travelling south into the panther country in the season of the crossing, Coinneach mac Mhàrtainn finds a whole valley emptied of flocks and every gate on the panthers' path standing open. An old herdswoman tells him the herders have kept the days of the crossing longer than any living memory can number, and ask no more of it than that.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <a href="#ev-III-0072"><em>The crossing days of the panthers</em>, 26 an t-Iuchar, LE 304</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3517"></a>**28 an t-Sultain, LE 304** — *Coinneach hears the carters' grumbling at An Leòmhann Buidhe* (An Leòmhann Buidhe). At the road-house of An Leòmhann Buidhe, Coinneach overhears a coal-carter complain that the northern galleries want two men to a face where one once sufficed, and begins, without deciding to, keeping a private count of how often the like is said to him on the road.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <a href="#ev-III-0073"><em>An Leòmhann Buidhe on the north road</em>, 24 an Lùnastal, LE 304</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3518"></a>**2 an t-Samhain, LE 305** — *Coinneach speaks with the teachers at Muileann chiar* (Coille Naomh Muileann chiar). In the sacred wood of Flidais at Muileann chiar, Coinneach tells the schools' elder teachers what he has gathered on the roads. Beathag nic Ruairidh names it a half question asked a thousand times, and tells him the schools want a fixed ground where it may be argued whole.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3519"></a>**4 an Dàmhair, LE 310** — *Coinneach walks the bounds of the schools' wood* (Coille Naomh Muileann chiar). Coinneach walks the boundary stones of the sacred wood at Muileann chiar alone, as the schools' teachers do once in a lifetime, and comes out of it resolved to build a fixed house for the question he has carried, rather than carry it hearth to hearth any longer.
- <a id="ev-III-0074"></a>**29 an Cèitean, LE 314** — *The house of disputation at Dùn thais* (Dùn thais). Coinneach mac Mhàrtainn, a druid of the schools of Flidais, lady of the deer, founds a house of disputation at Dùn thais, where the old question of the schools, Carson an làmh seo?, why the vein answers some hands and not others, is argued by rule. Pupils come from as far as Caol bheag.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-3518"><em>Coinneach speaks with the teachers at Muileann chiar</em>, 2 an t-Samhain, LE 305</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-3519"><em>Coinneach walks the bounds of the schools' wood</em>, 4 an Dàmhair, LE 310</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3520"></a>**2 an t-Samhain, LE 314** — *Taigh na Deasbaid raised at Dùn thais* (Dùn thais). Coinneach mac Mhàrtainn raises a hall of stone and turf at Dùn thais, Taigh na Deasbaid, and has the schools' old question, Carson an làmh seo?, cut into its lintel before the roof is finished. A rule is set: a question, once put, is argued a full year before any answer is given from the master's chair.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <a href="#ev-III-0074"><em>The house of disputation at Dùn thais</em>, 29 an Cèitean, LE 314</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3521"></a>**29 an t-Samhain, LE 318** — *Pupils come from Caol bheag* (Caol bheag). Word of the house at Dùn thais reaches the coast, and pupils begin walking three days from Caol bheag to sit its benches, sent by parents who have heard, by trader and carter, that a hard question is argued there properly. Among them is a fisherman's son, Aonghas mac Nèill, who stays to keep the house's register.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0074"><em>The house of disputation at Dùn thais</em>, 29 an Cèitean, LE 314</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3522"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, LE 320** — *Beathag nic Ruairidh visits the finished house* (Dùn thais). Beathag nic Ruairidh comes down from the grove of Muileann chiar to see the house Coinneach has built, walks its length in silence, and tells him afterward that the ground he has raised is fixed and patient enough, and asks only how long he means to let it argue safe things before he sets it the one question it was truly raised for.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0074"><em>The house of disputation at Dùn thais</em>, 29 an Cèitean, LE 314</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3523"></a>**26 am Faoilleach, LE 322** — *Birth of Uisdean mac Uisdein* (Cathair dhearg). A son, named Uisdean for his father, is born at Cathair dhearg to Uisdean mac Dhùghaill, then two-and-fifty years old and still waiting on his mother's long reign.
- <a id="ev-III-0075"></a>**1 an Giblean, LE 324** — *Coinneach's question* (Dùn thais). In open disputation Coinneach mac Mhàrtainn asks whether the hands that went with the fleet were those the vein answered best, and whether it now answers fewer. The seven houses forbid the question at their own tables; it is the first time they forbid a question and not a deed.
- <a id="ev-III-0076"></a>**30 an Giblean, LE 324** — *Baile Mòr mhòr grows* (Baile Mòr mhòr). After a run of poor seasons Baile Mòr mhòr on the northern plain takes in families from the upland farms and doubles within a generation. Its reeve divides the common grazing anew.
- <a id="ev-III-0077"></a>**27 an t-Ògmhios, LE 324** — *Death of Queen Sìleas* (Cathair dhearg). Queen Sìleas nic Fhearchair dies at Cathair dhearg after a reign of more than fifty years. Her son Uisdean mac Dhùghaill is crowned.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-3510"><em>Birth of Uisdean mac Dhùghaill</em>, 10 an t-Ògmhios, LE 270</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EIV-3523"><em>Birth of Uisdean mac Uisdein</em>, 26 am Faoilleach, LE 322</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3524"></a>**3 an Lùnastal, LE 324** — *Coinneach asks the forbidden question* (Dùn thais). Before a full hall at Dùn thais, Coinneach mac Mhàrtainn asks at last whether the hands that went with the fleet were those the vein answered best, and whether it answers fewer now. No one on the benches answers him, and he sets the question, unanswered, into the house's register.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0075"><em>Coinneach's question</em>, 1 an Giblean, LE 324</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3525"></a>**24 an Lùnastal, LE 324** — *The houses' ban carried to their tables*. Word of Coinneach's question travels shire to shire until it has reached every one of the seven custodian houses, and each in its own hall forbids the question at its own table: the first time the seven have forbidden a question rather than a deed.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0075"><em>Coinneach's question</em>, 1 an Giblean, LE 324</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3526"></a>**14 an t-Sultain, LE 324** — *The reeve divides the grazing at Baile Mòr mhòr anew* (Baile Mòr mhòr). After a run of poor upland seasons, Baile Mòr mhòr has taken in so many families from the failing farms that the town has all but doubled, and its reeve marks out shares of the common grazing for households that never held a share of it before.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0076"><em>Baile Mòr mhòr grows</em>, 30 an Giblean, LE 324</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3527"></a>**5 an Dàmhair, LE 324** — *Death of Queen Sìleas nic Fhearchair* (Cathair dhearg). Queen Sìleas nic Fhearchair dies at Cathair dhearg, one-and-eighty years old, in An Talla Dearg where she had reigned longer than any ruler before her, a reign of six-and-sixty years begun when she was crowned at fifteen, too young by the houses' own custom to take the crown at once.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <a href="#ev-III-0077"><em>Death of Queen Sìleas</em>, 27 an t-Ògmhios, LE 324</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3528"></a>**7 an Dùbhlachd, LE 324** — *Uisdean mac Dhùghaill crowned* (Cathair dhearg). Uisdean mac Dhùghaill, Sìleas's son, no young man himself by then, is crowned at Cathair dhearg in his mother's place before the season turns. The crown's scribes set his crowning and her death on the same board, one line after the other, as though the two were a single piece of news.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0077"><em>Death of Queen Sìleas</em>, 27 an t-Ògmhios, LE 324</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3529"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, LE 324** — *Coinneach walks home from the ban* (Dùn thais). Learning how Na Seachd Taighean have answered his question with a wider silence than his own, Coinneach mac Mhàrtainn walks the carters' road out from Dùn thais alone into the dark, and tells no pupil, then or after, what he has thought on the road.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-III-0075"><em>Coinneach's question</em>, 1 an Giblean, LE 324</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3530"></a>**24 am Màrt, LE 335** — *Iain mac Ùisdein set to his father's toll* (Drochaid Ros fhionn). A boy of Drochaid Ros fhionn is set to sit the bridge with the tally-stick and learn his letters between carts, the office his father and grandfather held before him over the stone crossing above Ros fhionn.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3531"></a>**27 an t-Sultain, LE 335** — *A reeve turns back from the pastures of Doire uaine before dark* (Marbh-bheò Doire uaine). A reeve sent from the shire seat to argue the shepherds of Doire uaine out of their custom of lighting no fires on the high pastures comes down again before dark the same day, and never returns to press the argument.
- <a id="ev-III-0078"></a>**2 an Gearran, LE 344** — *The deep hull that would not float true* (Inis àrsaidh). A merchant of Inis àrsaidh has a deep-keeled hull built for the long coast run eastward. The wrights no longer remember how Alasdair Saor scarfed his keels; the hull lists so badly at launch that it is broken up for timber.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3532"></a>**6 an t-Ògmhios, LE 344** — *Ruairidh mac Artair's deep hull built at Inis àrsaidh* (Inis àrsaidh). A merchant of Inis àrsaidh pays wrights to lay a deep-keeled hull for the long coast run, in the manner remembered of the fleet's own building. No wright of the day still holds the old scarfing of the keel timbers that let those hulls flex to a sea.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-III-0078"><em>The deep hull that would not float true</em>, 2 an Gearran, LE 344</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3533"></a>**7 an t-Ògmhios, LE 344** — *The hull that would not ride true* (Inis àrsaidh). Ruairidh's hull lists at launch past any righting and is broken up for timber within the fortnight; none of the old builders' lore of the keel's joinery survives among the wrights who raised her. No one is hurt in the breaking-up.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-III-0078"><em>The deep hull that would not float true</em>, 2 an Gearran, LE 344</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3534"></a>**8 an t-Ògmhios, LE 344** — *Coll of Inis àrsaidh on the lost scarfing*. Coll, the oldest wright at Inis àrsaidh, looks over Ruairidh mac Artair's listing hull and says that no wright now living holds the old joinery of the keel that let the fleet's hulls flex to a sea; nobody has asked for it in three hundred years.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0078"><em>The deep hull that would not float true</em>, 2 an Gearran, LE 344</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3535"></a>**29 an t-Samhain, LE 350** — *Brine springs found on the flats above Ros fhionn* (Ros fhionn). A farmer digging a drainage ditch above Ros fhionn strikes warm water that tastes of salt. Within a season the district's own folk have laid out shallow pans on the flats to catch the brine.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3536"></a>**31 an Dàmhair, LE 352** — *Death of Uisdean mac Dhùghaill* (Cathair dhearg). Uisdean mac Dhùghaill dies at Cathair dhearg in his two-and-eightieth year, and his son Uisdean mac Uisdein, already thirty, is crowned without dispute. The tidings reach the northern flats by a rider bound for the shire seat.
- <a id="ev-III-0079"></a>**3 am Màrt, LE 354** — *Salt pans at Ros fhionn* (Ros fhionn). The river town of Ros fhionn in the north-east lays out salt pans at the brine springs on its river flats and sends salt inland over Drochaid Ros fhionn. Within a generation Ros fhionn salt is the common measure of worth in the north-eastern shires.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-3535"><em>Brine springs found on the flats above Ros fhionn</em>, 29 an t-Samhain, LE 350</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0080"></a>**18 an t-Sultain, LE 361** — *The wool of Baile gharbh* (Baile gharbh). The weavers of Baile gharbh make a heavy undyed cloth that sheds rain, and it becomes the common cloak of the north-east. In this cloth the white sorrow is kept.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3537"></a>**8 an Dùbhlachd, LE 361** — *Baile gharbh's rain-cloth worn for mourning in the north-east* (Baile gharbh). The heavy undyed cloth of Baile gharbh, already the common rain-cloak of the north-east, becomes the district's own cloth of mourning, worn plain and undyed through a household's season of loss as the whole island once wore an Tùrsa Geal.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-III-0080"><em>The wool of Baile gharbh</em>, 18 an t-Sultain, LE 361</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0081"></a>**20 an Lùnastal, LE 369** — *Salt over Drochaid Ros fhionn* (Drochaid Ros fhionn). So many salt carts cross Drochaid Ros fhionn that the bridge-keeper is granted a handful from each load. His salt-box is said to hold more than some villages' granaries.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3538"></a>**29 an t-Samhain, LE 369** — *The bridge-keeper granted a handful from every load* (Drochaid Ros fhionn). The shire seat grants the keeper of Drochaid Ros fhionn a handful of salt from every load crossing the bridge, in place of any other toll. Iain mac Ùisdein keeps the due honestly and becomes known along the road for it.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-III-0081"><em>Salt over Drochaid Ros fhionn</em>, 20 an Lùnastal, LE 369</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3539"></a>**5 an Lùnastal, LE 372** — *Birth of Aonghas mac Uisdein* (Cathair dhearg). A son, Aonghas, is born at Cathair dhearg to Uisdean mac Uisdein in the twentieth year of his reign, when the king is fifty years old.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3540"></a>**16 an Gearran, LE 375** — *The bridge-keeper's salt-box* (Drochaid Ros fhionn). Iain mac Ùisdein builds an iron-bound oak box beside his stool to hold his due of salt. It fills faster than any box on that road was thought able to fill, and carters along the way say it holds more against a hard winter than some whole villages.
- <a id="ev-III-0082"></a>**27 an Cèitean, LE 379** — *The wells crack at Cill ghlas* (Scàineadh Cill ghlas). An earth tremor in the hills about Cill ghlas cracks three wells and brings down a byre. The custodians of the vein-house note it, and note that the galleries were untouched.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3541"></a>**14 an t-Sultain, LE 379** — *The wells crack at Cill ghlas* (Cill ghlas). An earth tremor cracks three wells and brings down a byre at Cill ghlas. The custodians of Taigh na Fèithe send men into the galleries below and find the deep workings untouched, though the diggers speak among themselves of feeling the shaking reach them under the hill.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-III-0082"><em>The wells crack at Cill ghlas</em>, 27 an Cèitean, LE 379</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3542"></a>**20 an t-Iuchar, LE 380** — *Taigh na Fèithe offers stone for Cill ghlas's byre* (Cill ghlas). The custodians of Taigh na Fèithe offer stone from their own surplus to rebuild the byre brought down at Cill ghlas, a kindness the village does not forget.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3543"></a>**18 an Lùnastal, LE 380** — *Mòr nic Nèill made tutor to the king's son* (Cathair dhearg). Mòr nic Nèill is set over the young Aonghas mac Uisdein to teach him his letters as a child, the first time any heir to An Talla Dearg has been given a tutor for the purpose rather than left to pick up his letters between other business.
- <a id="ev-III-0083"></a>**26 an Giblean, LE 394** — *The Hollow Man spoken of again* (Marbh-bheò Doire uaine). The shepherds of the Doire uaine hills will light no fires on the high pastures, for the old inscriptions of Marbh-bheò Doire uaine. A reeve sent from Muileann chiar to make them see sense does not stay the night.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-3531"><em>A reeve turns back from the pastures of Doire uaine before dark</em>, 27 an t-Sultain, LE 335</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0084"></a>**25 an Cèitean, LE 394** — *Aonghas mac Uisdein crowned* (Cathair dhearg). Uisdean mac Uisdein dies, the son of Uisdean mac Dhùghaill and king after him, and his own son Aonghas mac Uisdein is crowned at Cathair dhearg, a young man of twenty-two. Aonghas is the first king to learn his letters as a child.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EIV-3539"><em>Birth of Aonghas mac Uisdein</em>, 5 an Lùnastal, LE 372</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0085"></a>**23 an t-Ògmhios, LE 394** — *Àth fhiadhaich salt fish* (Àth fhiadhaich). Àth fhiadhaich begins to salt its catch with Ros fhionn salt and send it inland to the mining towns. From this time the mining shires eat salt fish in the lean season.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3544"></a>**28 an Lùnastal, LE 394** — *Death of Uisdean mac Uisdein and the crowning of Aonghas* (Cathair dhearg). Uisdean mac Uisdein dies at two-and-seventy after two-and-forty years in the hall. His son Aonghas, two-and-twenty and taught his letters as a child, is crowned at Cathair dhearg with less dispute than any crowning in living memory.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-III-0084"><em>Aonghas mac Uisdein crowned</em>, 25 an Cèitean, LE 394</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3545"></a>**9 an t-Sultain, LE 394** — *Àth fhiadhaich turns to Ros fhionn salt* (Àth fhiadhaich). The fishing town of Àth fhiadhaich, having lost catch to poor curing, begins sending carts north for Ros fhionn salt. From this year the mining shires to the south eat their salt fish cured with salt carried over Drochaid Ros fhionn.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-III-0085"><em>Àth fhiadhaich salt fish</em>, 23 an t-Ògmhios, LE 394</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3546"></a>**26 am Màrt, LE 400** — *Birth of Aonghas Òg* (Cathair dhearg). A son, named Aonghas for his father, is born at Cathair dhearg to King Aonghas mac Uisdein, eight-and-twenty years old and six years crowned.

## The Years LE 401 – 500

- <a id="ev-EIV-3547"></a>**6 an t-Sultain, LE 403** — *An old watching family questions Dòmhnall mac Ailein's right to name the stone* (Inis thais). One of the families who have kept watch on the wolf-stone at Inis thais for generations sends its eldest to ask a net-maker preaching on the strand what right he has to put a new name on their old duty. He answers that he claims no watch of his own and has only said aloud what the family's own hands have been doing unnamed for years.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3548"></a>**6 an Cèitean, LE 405** — *Dòmhnall mac Ailein's first preaching on the strand* (Inis thais). A net-maker of Inis thais, thirty-five years old, begins telling the men who mend nets beside him that the town's old wolf-stone is Lia Fàil, and that its watching families are an Fhianna, sworn to keep the whole island as a wolf keeps its range. His hearers grow through the year into the first gathering of Òrd na Cloiche at Inis thais.
- <a id="ev-III-0086"></a>**28 am Màrt, LE 409** — *Clach first preached at Inis thais* (Inis thais). Dòmhnall mac Ailein, a net-maker of Inis thais, where the wolf-sworn's stone Clach stands, preaches that the stone is Lia Fàil, which cries out under the rightful king, and that its sworn guards are the Fianna, who keep the island as a wolf keeps its range. His hearers are the first congregation of Òrd na Cloiche, the order of the Stone.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-3547"><em>An old watching family questions Dòmhnall mac Ailein's right to name the stone</em>, 6 an t-Sultain, LE 403</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-3548"><em>Dòmhnall mac Ailein's first preaching on the strand</em>, 6 an Cèitean, LE 405</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3549"></a>**12 an t-Iuchar, LE 415** — *A shipmaster of Inis thais sails north for slate* (Inis thais). Beathag nic Raoghnaill, a shipmaster who has carried wool and hides along the southern coast for twenty years, offers to fetch roofing slate for the wolf-stone's new hall herself rather than trust the errand to another. She returns a season later with a hull low under northern slate.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3550"></a>**10 an Cèitean, LE 418** — *Slate brought by sea for the temple at Inis thais* (Inis thais). The northern slate Beathag nic Raoghnaill brought south is laid over the wolf-stone's new hall, the first roof on that coast built to outlast its own builder. The town remarks as much on the roof's cost as on its wonder.
- <a id="ev-III-0087"></a>**16 an Dùbhlachd, LE 419** — *The wolf-house at Inis thais* (Inis thais). The followers of Dòmhnall mac Ailein raise at Inis thais the first temple on the island to Lia Fàil by name. It is roofed with slate brought by sea from the north.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-3549"><em>A shipmaster of Inis thais sails north for slate</em>, 12 an t-Iuchar, LE 415</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-3550"><em>Slate brought by sea for the temple at Inis thais</em>, 10 an Cèitean, LE 418</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3551"></a>**11 an Giblean, LE 420** — *The tide-horn of the wolf-stone shrine* (Inis thais). An Fhianna at Inis thais take up a horn blown at every turn of the tide, its blowing passed by lot among the watching households. Within a few years the town sets its morning's business by the horn without a thought for what it was first blown to mark.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3552"></a>**7 an t-Iuchar, LE 421** — *The naming of Lia Fàil carried inland by a hide-trader* (Inis thais). A fisherman of Inis thais who has heard Dòmhnall mac Ailein twice repeats the naming of Lia Fàil to three inland villages while selling hides that winter, none of which he visits again. The teaching spreads in threads too small to trace to their source.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-III-0086"><em>Clach first preached at Inis thais</em>, 28 am Màrt, LE 409</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3553"></a>**19 am Faoilleach, LE 427** — *Òrd an t-Seabhaig and an Fhianna claim the same feast day at Caol leathan* (Caol leathan). The priests of Òrd an t-Seabhaig and an Fhianna both come to the harbour shrine at Caol leathan for the same morning's hours, Òrd an t-Seabhaig's reckoning and Òrd na Cloiche's vigil falling that year on the same day. Neither will give way.
- <a id="ev-III-0088"></a>**29 am Faoilleach, LE 429** — *Hawk and wolf at Caol leathan* (Caol leathan). The priests of the Hawk and the Fianna of the Stone both claim the harbour shrine at Caol leathan. The king's reeve divides its days between them, as the sacred woods were divided in the Holy Age, and the division holds.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-3553"><em>Òrd an t-Seabhaig and an Fhianna claim the same feast day at Caol leathan</em>, 19 am Faoilleach, LE 427</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3554"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, LE 429** — *Murchadh mac Ailpein divides the shrine's days* (Caol leathan). The king's reeve at Caol leathan, Murchadh mac Ailpein, halves the harbour shrine's hours between Òrd an t-Seabhaig and an Fhianna, as the sacred woods of an older age were once divided, and nails the division on a strip of hide to the shrine door.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-III-0088"><em>Hawk and wolf at Caol leathan</em>, 29 am Faoilleach, LE 429</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0088a"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, LE 435** — *The market inside the new gate* (Seann Skell). Seann Skell on the Hawk bay is walled, and a market is granted inside the new landward gate, where amber, whale-oil, honey and the sheep of the northern moors are sold. The amber-workers of the bay swear to sell no rough amber outside the walls.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3555"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, LE 435** — *Birth of Iain mac Aonghais* (Cathair dhearg). A son, Iain, is born at Cathair dhearg to Aonghas Òg, the king's heir, then five-and-thirty years old; the old king, sixty-three, sees his grandson named at the yoke-poles of Macha's rite.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3556"></a>**31 an Dàmhair, LE 436** — *Ailig an Òir forfeits a season's amber* (Seann Skell). An amber-worker of Seann Skell on Bàgh an t-Seabhaig is caught selling rough amber outside the new walls against his own guild's oath, and is made by that guild to forfeit the whole season's gathering to the market fund rather than face the crown's reeve.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-III-0088a"><em>The market inside the new gate</em>, 28 an Dùbhlachd, LE 435</a>.</span>
