- <a id="ev-EIV-3557"></a>**2 an Dàmhair, LE 440** — *Death of Dòmhnall mac Ailein* (Inis thais). Dòmhnall mac Ailein dies at Inis thais in his seventieth year, having taught on the strand five-and-thirty years without ever taking up an office in the order his hearers named after his teaching. An Fhianna carry him to the shrine and set him before it, not within it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0086"><em>Clach first preached at Inis thais</em>, 28 am Màrt, LE 409</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0089"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, LE 441** — *Macha at court* (Cathair dhearg). King Aonghas takes up the wood-watchers' rite of Macha, which keeps the two horses of one chariot, foaled on one night, Liath Macha the grey and Dubh Sainglenn the black: two horses, one yoke, light and dark two powers in balance, and the vein belonging to both. The court follows him, and Òrd Mhacha, the order of Macha, becomes the order of Cathair dhearg and the crown.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-3558"><em>King Aonghas recalls his father's teaching on the two horses</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, LE 441</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-3559"><em>A councillor warns Aonghas against Òrd Mhacha' rite</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, LE 441</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3558"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, LE 441** — *King Aonghas recalls his father's teaching on the two horses* (Cathair dhearg). Before he takes up Òrd Mhacha' rite himself, King Aonghas mac Uisdein recalls being told as a boy that one horse pulling alone draws a chariot only in a circle, and that it takes two, pulling together and never quite agreeing, to pull it straight.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-III-0089"><em>Macha at court</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, LE 441</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3559"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, LE 441** — *A councillor warns Aonghas against Òrd Mhacha' rite* (Cathair dhearg). An old councillor of An Talla Dearg warns King Aonghas that a crown seen at a moor-custom may be asked by Na Seachd Taighean why it will not be seen at theirs. Aonghas answers that any house is free to come and stand at a yoke-pole itself.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-III-0089"><em>Macha at court</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, LE 441</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3560"></a>**3 an Dàmhair, LE 442** — *Half An Talla Dearg's household takes up the rite of Macha* (Cathair dhearg). Within a year of King Aonghas standing at the yoke-pole of Òrd Mhacha' rite, half his own household has taken it up beside him, and Òrd Mhacha becomes from that year the order of Cathair dhearg without a quarrel fought over it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0089"><em>Macha at court</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, LE 441</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-3561"></a>**24 am Faoilleach, LE 446** — *A quarryman's household first roofs in slate at Tobar dhearg* (Tobar dhearg). A family burned out in the fire at Tobar dhearg, a quarryman among them, is the first in the village to roof again in slate rather than thatch, judging that a man who cuts the stone has less excuse than his neighbours to sleep under straw.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3562"></a>**9 an Gearran, LE 446** — *The crown sends grain south after the fire at Tobar dhearg* (Cathair dhearg). King Aonghas sends what the crown's granaries can spare south to Tobar dhearg before the winter closes the roads, the village having lost most of its stores along with its roofs.
- <a id="ev-EIV-3563"></a>**16 am Màrt, LE 446** — *King Aonghas returns to the yoke a second year* (Cathair dhearg). King Aonghas rides out to Òrd Mhacha' rite a second spring running, judging that a thing done once by a king and not again is no rite at all, and stands again with a hand on each yoke-pole among the grey horse and the black.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0089"><em>Macha at court</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, LE 441</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0090"></a>**28 am Màrt, LE 446** — *Fire at Tobar dhearg* (Tobar dhearg). Fire runs through the thatch of Tobar dhearg and burns most of the village. It is rebuilt with slate from the quarries nearby, and is known thereafter for its slate roofs.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIV-3561"><em>A quarryman's household first roofs in slate at Tobar dhearg</em>, 24 am Faoilleach, LE 446</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-3562"><em>The crown sends grain south after the fire at Tobar dhearg</em>, 9 an Gearran, LE 446</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4001"></a>**21 am Faoilleach, LE 450** — *Death of King Aonghas mac Uisdein* (Cathair dhearg). King Aonghas mac Uisdein dies at Cathair dhearg in his seventy-eighth year, after six-and-fifty years crowned, having set Òrd Mhacha' rite of Macha as the crown's own custom. Leabhar a' Chùraim gives him one line: the name, the year, and no more.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0089"><em>Macha at court</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, LE 441</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4002"></a>**18 an Giblean, LE 450** — *Aonghas Òg crowned at fifty* (Cathair dhearg). Aonghas Òg mac Aonghais is crowned at Cathair dhearg the same season his father dies, fifty years old and no young man, for all his name.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0089"><em>Macha at court</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, LE 441</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4003"></a>**19 an Gearran, LE 460** — *Eilidh Dhubh begins to teach at Doire chiar* (Doire chiar). Eilidh nic Iain, taught in secret by her grandmother, begins to say aloud at Doire chiar the old teaching that the vein answers labour and not birth. She sets it down in a hand her mother taught her, and pupils begin to copy it for households too far off to hear her speak.
- <a id="ev-EIV-4004"></a>**24 an t-Samhain, LE 460** — *Birth of Tormod Bàn* (Cathair dhearg). A son, Tormod, fair-haired from the cradle and so called Tormod Bàn, is born at Cathair dhearg to Iain mac Aonghais, five-and-twenty years old, in the tenth year of his grandfather Aonghas Òg's reign.
- <a id="ev-III-0091"></a>**14 am Faoilleach, LE 471** — *Macha's priests in Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag* (Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag). The custody of Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag, shared since the Holy Age, passes by royal grant to the priests of Macha. The other claimants leave the wood without contest. Why is not told.
- <a id="ev-EIV-4005"></a>**16 am Faoilleach, LE 471** — *Macha's priests granted Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag* (Cnoc bheag). The custody of Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag, held in common since An Aois Naomh, passes by royal grant to the priests of Macha alone. The other claimants withdraw from the wood the same season without contest; why they go so quietly is not told.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0091"><em>Macha's priests in Coille Naomh Cnoc bheag</em>, 14 am Faoilleach, LE 471</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4006"></a>**21 an Lùnastal, LE 471** — *Taigh na Fèithe orders every copy of the tracts given up* (Muileann dhearg). Word of Eilidh Dhubh's tracts reaches the custodians' galleries at Muileann dhearg, and Taigh na Fèithe orders every copy brought in and given up, promising no penalty to any household that surrenders one freely before the season's end.
- <a id="ev-EIV-4007"></a>**8 an Dùbhlachd, LE 471** — *Some hundred tracts burned in Taigh na Fèithe yard* (Muileann dhearg). Carriers gather some hundred hides and boards of Eilidh Dhubh's tracts from households across the north-east and burn them in Taigh na Fèithe yard at Muileann dhearg before the gathered custodians. Eilidh walks from Doire chiar to see it done, and says nothing.
- <a id="ev-EIV-4008"></a>**19 an Dàmhair, LE 475** — *A harvest gathering at Muileann chiar hears the tracts read* (Muileann chiar). Coinneach Odhar, taught his letters by Eilidh Dhubh to carry her teaching where she will not travel, reads the tracts aloud for the first time at a harvest gathering near Muileann chiar. Not every household takes to it easily, and a farmer's wife elsewhere warns that the teaching could get colliers killed.
- <a id="ev-III-0092"></a>**11 an t-Iuchar, LE 479** — *The druid schools keep Coille Naomh Muileann chiar* (Coille Naomh Muileann chiar). The druids of the schools take the keeping of Coille Naomh Muileann chiar, the wood of Flidais's white stag, and walk its bounds each year. The walk becomes the one open rite of the schools.
- <a id="ev-EIV-4009"></a>**11 an Dùbhlachd, LE 479** — *Scoiltean nan Draoidhean take up the walk of Coille Naomh Muileann chiar* (Muileann chiar). Scoiltean nan Draoidhean, holding no ground of their own since An Aois Naomh, take up the yearly keeping of Coille Naomh Muileann chiar at Muileann chiar, walking its bounds in a procession that grows within a decade into the one rite the schools still keep open to any who will walk with them.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0092"><em>The druid schools keep Coille Naomh Muileann chiar</em>, 11 an t-Iuchar, LE 479</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0093"></a>**29 am Faoilleach, LE 484** — *The drovers of Àth chiar* (Àth chiar). Drovers of Àth chiar begin to drive cattle each year over the eastern hills to the mining towns. Theirs are the first roads on the island marked with cairns.
- <a id="ev-III-0094"></a>**23 an t-Ògmhios, LE 484** — *Eilidh Dhubh's tracts* (Doire chiar). At Doire chiar Eilidh nic Iain, called Eilidh Dhubh, wakes again the teaching of the rival school of the Holy Age, that the vein answers labour and not birth, and sets it out in tracts that her pupils copy. The tracts are read aloud at harvest gatherings across the north-east.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-4003"><em>Eilidh Dhubh begins to teach at Doire chiar</em>, 19 an Gearran, LE 460</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-4008"><em>A harvest gathering at Muileann chiar hears the tracts read</em>, 19 an Dàmhair, LE 475</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0095"></a>**2 an Dùbhlachd, LE 484** — *The tracts burned at Muileann dhearg* (Muileann dhearg). The vein-house commands every copy of Eilidh Dhubh's tracts brought to Muileann dhearg and burned, and some hundred are given up. Eilidh is not punished. She dies at Doire chiar, still teaching.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-4006"><em>Taigh na Fèithe orders every copy of the tracts given up</em>, 21 an Lùnastal, LE 471</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-4007"><em>Some hundred tracts burned in Taigh na Fèithe yard</em>, 8 an Dùbhlachd, LE 471</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0096"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, LE 484** — *Death of King Aonghas* (Cathair dhearg). King Aonghas Òg, son of Aonghas mac Uisdein and crowned after him, dies at Cathair dhearg and is buried by the rite of Macha, the first king so buried. His son Iain mac Aonghais is crowned.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EIV-3546"><em>Birth of Aonghas Òg</em>, 26 am Màrt, LE 400</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIV-4010"><em>King Aonghas Òg buried by the rite of Macha</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, LE 484</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIV-4012"><em>Iain mac Aonghais crowned at nine-and-forty</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, LE 484</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4010"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, LE 484** — *King Aonghas Òg buried by the rite of Macha* (Cathair dhearg). King Aonghas Òg dies in the winter of his eighty-fourth year and is carried to his grave at Cathair dhearg by Òrd Mhacha' rite of Macha, the first king of the line so buried. His household stands at the yoke-poles of the two horses he rode out to see brought up together every spring of his reign.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0096"><em>Death of King Aonghas</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, LE 484</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4011"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, LE 484** — *The drovers of Àth chiar raise the first cairns* (Àth chiar). The drovers who drive cattle each year from Àth chiar over the eastern hills to the mining towns begin marking their road with a cairn at every day's stage, the first roads on the island so marked, so that a beast lost in mist or a driver new to the trade may find the way again unasked.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0093"><em>The drovers of Àth chiar</em>, 29 am Faoilleach, LE 484</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4012"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, LE 484** — *Iain mac Aonghais crowned at nine-and-forty* (Cathair dhearg). Iain mac Aonghais is crowned at Cathair dhearg after his father Aonghas Òg is carried to his grave by Macha's rite, nine-and-forty years old, with three sons living.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0096"><em>Death of King Aonghas</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, LE 484</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4013"></a>**17 an t-Sultain, LE 485** — *A hidden copy of the tracts kept at Doire chiar* (Doire chiar). A single hide of the tracts, in Eilidh Dhubh's mother's own hand, is kept whole in a hollow beam of Eilidh's house, given to no household but her own kin's. Eilidh shows it to no one outside her family, judging it kept for her mother's sake more than the country's.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0095"><em>The tracts burned at Muileann dhearg</em>, 2 an Dùbhlachd, LE 484</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4014"></a>**13 an Dùbhlachd, LE 490** — *Birth of Dùghall, Iain mac Aonghais's son by his second wife* (Cathair dhearg). King Iain mac Aonghais, his first wife some years dead, takes a second wife who bears him a third son, Dùghall, the first of his three sons born at An Talla Dearg itself under a crown his father already wears.
- <a id="ev-III-0097"></a>**27 an Gearran, LE 496** — *Tormod Bàn crowned* (Cathair dhearg). Iain mac Aonghais dies after a short reign, and his son Tormod mac Iain, called Tormod Bàn for his white hair, is crowned at Cathair dhearg. The houses swear to him without dispute.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EIV-3555"><em>Birth of Iain mac Aonghais</em>, 30 an Dùbhlachd, LE 435</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EIV-4004"><em>Birth of Tormod Bàn</em>, 24 an t-Samhain, LE 460</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-4014"><em>Birth of Dùghall, Iain mac Aonghais's son by his second wife</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, LE 490</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4015"></a>**7 am Màrt, LE 496** — *Death of King Iain mac Aonghais* (Cathair dhearg). King Iain mac Aonghais dies at Cathair dhearg at one-and-sixty, twelve years crowned, the third king An Talla Dearg has buried in a single generation. His second son Aonghas, nineteen, stands a pace back from the hall's centre at his brother Tormod's crowning.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-III-0097"><em>Tormod Bàn crowned</em>, 27 an Gearran, LE 496</a>.</span>

## The Years LE 501 – 600

- <a id="ev-EIV-4016"></a>**9 an Gearran, LE 505** — *Death of Eilidh Dhubh* (Doire chiar). Eilidh nic Iain, Eilidh Dhubh, dies at Doire chiar in her seventy-fifth year, still teaching within the hour of her death. Her pupils raise no stone over her, and Coinneach Odhar reads the tracts aloud at her graveside from the copy he has carried thirty years.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0095"><em>The tracts burned at Muileann dhearg</em>, 2 an Dùbhlachd, LE 484</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0098"></a>**8 an Lùnastal, LE 509** — *Winter at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr* (An Taigh-seinnse Mòr). An Taigh-seinnse Mòr on the central mining road becomes the house where the ox-teams of the mountain wait out the worst of the snow. Its keeper, Iain mac Mhurchaidh, builds them a second byre and keeps a book of the teams that lodged.
- <a id="ev-EIV-4017"></a>**28 an Dàmhair, LE 509** — *Iain mac Mhurchaidh raises a second byre at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr* (An Taigh-seinnse Mòr). Iain mac Mhurchaidh, keeper of the road-house at the halfway stage of the central mining road, raises a second byre against the growing traffic of the ox-teams and begins a careful book of every team that lodges there through the mountain snows.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0098"><em>Winter at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr</em>, 8 an Lùnastal, LE 509</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0099"></a>**6 an t-Sultain, LE 514** — *The bell-founders of Muileann naomh* (Muileann naomh). A family of Muileann naomh casts the first bronze bell on Dia-thìr to hang in a hawk-house. It cracks in its first frost; the second holds.
- <a id="ev-EIV-4018"></a>**1 an Gearran, LE 515** — *The second bell of Muileann naomh holds* (Muileann naomh). After the first bell cast for the hawk-house at Muileann naomh cracks in its first frost, the founders cast a second, thicker at the waist, and it holds, ringing thereafter at every measured burning kept at the house and at every turn of the coast's own reckoning of the year besides.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0099"><em>The bell-founders of Muileann naomh</em>, 6 an t-Sultain, LE 514</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0100"></a>**5 am Màrt, LE 519** — *An Gàire Dubh* (Cuan dhearg). A storm named in the south-coast rolls An Gàire Dubh, the Black Laugh, drives the sea over the waterfront of Cuan dhearg and spoils the season's salt fish. The town is built again a street further from the shore.
- <a id="ev-EIV-4019"></a>**6 am Màrt, LE 519** — *Tormod Bàn hears the tidings of An Gàire Dubh standing* (Cathair dhearg). Word of the sea driven over the waterfront of Cuan dhearg reaches An Talla Dearg nine days late by a rider who has ridden two horses to death. King Tormod Bàn, nine-and-fifty, hears it standing, as his scribes note he does only when a report troubles him past sitting.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0100"><em>An Gàire Dubh</em>, 5 am Màrt, LE 519</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4020"></a>**31 am Màrt, LE 519** — *The king sends grain south unasked* (Cuan dhearg). Before the roads close for the winter King Tormod Bàn sends grain south to Cuan dhearg, though its reeve has sent no asking, only the bare report of the water; the season's salt fish had spoiled on the racks below the town.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0100"><em>An Gàire Dubh</em>, 5 am Màrt, LE 519</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4021"></a>**5 an Cèitean, LE 520** — *Cuan dhearg rebuilds a street back from the shore* (Cuan dhearg). After An Gàire Dubh drowns its waterfront, Cuan dhearg of the red cliffs rebuilds a full street back from the old shoreline, on ground no telling the town keeps says the sea has ever reached, and the new street holds.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0100"><em>An Gàire Dubh</em>, 5 am Màrt, LE 519</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4022"></a>**3 an t-Ògmhios, LE 521** — *King Tormod visits Cuan dhearg's new street* (Cuan dhearg). King Tormod Bàn rides to Cuan dhearg to see its rebuilt street, the one journey of his reign made, his own scribes note, for a storm's sake alone rather than for a war, a crowning or a rite the crown was bound to keep.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0100"><em>An Gàire Dubh</em>, 5 am Màrt, LE 519</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4023"></a>**2 an t-Iuchar, LE 525** — *A reciter of Clann na Ceiste says Clann a' Chlachair at a naming* (Tobar dhìreach). At a naming among the wells of Tobar dhìreach, for a steward's son of the king's own household, the reciter Muireach mac Ailein says the line of An Clachair over the child rather than the long line of Somhairle that royal namings there have called on for generations.
- <a id="ev-III-0101"></a>**13 an t-Sultain, LE 526** — *The hawk-house at Muileann naomh* (Muileann naomh). Muileann naomh in the south becomes the southernmost house of the Hawk, and rings its bell at each measured burning. There the Hawk's teaching holds when it fades elsewhere in the south.
- <a id="ev-EIV-4024"></a>**2 an Dàmhair, LE 526** — *Birth of Catrìona nic Aonghais at Inis thais* (Inis thais). A daughter, Catrìona, is born at Inis thais to Aonghas mac Iain, the king's brother, and his wife Mairead nic Ailein, the first child of that marriage to live past her own naming. King Tormod Bàn rides down himself to see her named.
- <a id="ev-EIV-4025"></a>**28 an t-Ògmhios, LE 527** — *Muileann naomh draws pilgrims from further south* (Muileann naomh). Word of the hawk-house at Muileann naomh, where the old teaching is still given whole and unsoftened, carries south along the coast, and pilgrims begin to come to it from towns further south than any hawk-house had drawn from before.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0101"><em>The hawk-house at Muileann naomh</em>, 13 an t-Sultain, LE 526</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4026"></a>**27 an t-Sultain, LE 530** — *Death of Aonghas mac Iain* (Inis thais). Aonghas mac Iain, the king's brother, dies at Inis thais in his fifty-fourth year of a wasting sickness, King Tormod Bàn having ridden down to sit with him three days before the end. He is buried in the ground of that coast, at his own household's asking.
- <a id="ev-EIV-4027"></a>**20 an t-Ògmhios, LE 531** — *Mairead nic Ailein keeps her daughter from An Talla Dearg* (Inis thais). Offered a place under the king's own roof for her widowed household, Mairead nic Ailein keeps her daughter Catrìona at Inis thais rather than raise her at Cathair dhearg, judging a fatherless girl better raised among neighbours than as a king's ward with an unnamed claim.
- <a id="ev-III-0102"></a>**18 an t-Ògmhios, LE 534** — *The king's sons drowned in Abhainn fhionn* (Abhainn fhionn). Both sons of King Tormod Bàn drown when a ferry overturns on Abhainn fhionn in spate. The king has no other child.
- <a id="ev-EIV-4028"></a>**25 an Dàmhair, LE 534** — *Iain Odhar cleared of blame for the ferry* (Abhainn fhionn). The ferryman Iain Odhar comes before the king's reeves to answer for the ferry's overturning, and is cleared: he judged the spate as he had judged the river a hundred times before, and no such flood had come down that crossing unwarned in his eleven years on the rope.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0102"><em>The king's sons drowned in Abhainn fhionn</em>, 18 an t-Ògmhios, LE 534</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4029"></a>**13 an t-Samhain, LE 534** — *A new ferry ordered a mile upstream* (Abhainn fhionn). King Tormod Bàn has the old ferry rope cut and burned and orders a second crossing built a mile upstream, where the ford-keepers judge the river safer in spate, and never crosses the Abhainn fhionn again without a rider sent ahead to test the current.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0102"><em>The king's sons drowned in Abhainn fhionn</em>, 18 an t-Ògmhios, LE 534</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4030"></a>**17 an t-Samhain, LE 535** — *Iain Odhar made keeper of the new crossing* (Abhainn fhionn). The king grants Iain Odhar a small holding above the new crossing, not as payment for the two lives the old ferry took, but as a keeper's fee, and the ferryman watches the new rope closely for the thirty years he has left to keep it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0102"><em>The king's sons drowned in Abhainn fhionn</em>, 18 an t-Ògmhios, LE 534</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4031"></a>**29 an Lùnastal, LE 538** — *The three nearest the crown reckoned* (Muileann dhearg). In the fourth year after the ferry, the custodians of Taigh na Fèithe cease to reckon quietly who stands nearest the crown: Dùghall Garbh the king's half-brother, Catrìona nic Aonghais his niece, and Raghnall Ruadh of Clann Raghnaill.
- <a id="ev-EIV-4032"></a>**31 an t-Iuchar, LE 540** — *Raghnall Ruadh made master of Taigh na Fèithe* (Muileann dhearg). The custodians of Taigh na Fèithe at Muileann dhearg choose Raghnall Ruadh, head of Clann Raghnaill, as master over two men of longer service, judging that Taigh na Fèithe, which may soon answer to no clear crown, had better answer to the steadiest hand at hand.
- <a id="ev-EIV-4033"></a>**2 an t-Iuchar, LE 541** — *A councillor asks King Tormod to name an heir* (Cathair dhearg). An old councillor of An Talla Dearg asks King Tormod Bàn, seven years after the ferry, whether he means to name one of the three standing nearest the crown before age chooses in his place. The king answers that he will hold the crown himself while breath allows it.
- <a id="ev-III-0103"></a>**8 an t-Sultain, LE 547** — *Death of Tormod Bàn* (Cathair dhearg). King Tormod Bàn dies at Cathair dhearg without naming an heir, and three claims are laid before the houses at once.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-4033"><em>A councillor asks King Tormod to name an heir</em>, 2 an t-Iuchar, LE 541</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4034"></a>**14 an Dàmhair, LE 547** — *Tormod Bàn's last order* (Cathair dhearg). Dying at Cathair dhearg at seven-and-eighty, one-and-fifty years crowned, King Tormod Bàn gives his last clear order to the scribe beside him: that the boundary dispute at Àth chiar, unsettled after three seasons, go to the custodians to finish.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0103"><em>Death of Tormod Bàn</em>, 8 an t-Sultain, LE 547</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4035"></a>**23 an Dùbhlachd, LE 548** — *The houses hold the hall in common* (Cathair dhearg). Unable to agree on any one of the three claims laid before them, Na Seachd Taighean hold An Talla Dearg in common, the custodians sitting together in the crown's stead and keeping the kingdom's small business moving while the larger question of the crown stands unanswered.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0103"><em>Death of Tormod Bàn</em>, 8 an t-Sultain, LE 547</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0104"></a>**21 an Giblean, LE 552** — *The three claimants* (Cathair dhearg). The crown is claimed by Catrìona nic Aonghais of Inis thais, niece of the late king; by Dùghall Garbh of Baile Mòr dhomhain, his half-brother; and by Raghnall Ruadh, head of Clann Raghnaill and master of the vein-house. The seven houses divide among them, and the War of the Three Claimants begins.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-4024"><em>Birth of Catrìona nic Aonghais at Inis thais</em>, 2 an Dàmhair, LE 526</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-4026"><em>Death of Aonghas mac Iain</em>, 27 an t-Sultain, LE 530</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-4027"><em>Mairead nic Ailein keeps her daughter from An Talla Dearg</em>, 20 an t-Ògmhios, LE 531</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-4031"><em>The three nearest the crown reckoned</em>, 29 an Lùnastal, LE 538</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-4032"><em>Raghnall Ruadh made master of Taigh na Fèithe</em>, 31 an t-Iuchar, LE 540</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-4035"><em>The houses hold the hall in common</em>, 23 an Dùbhlachd, LE 548</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4036"></a>**16 an t-Sultain, LE 552** — *Mairead nic Ruairidh bars the gate to all three* (Seann Warr). The heralds of Catrìona nic Aonghais, Dùghall Garbh and Raghnall Ruadh come one after another to the western gate of Seann Warr, and its reeve Mairead nic Ruairidh gives each the same answer: the town will open to trade and shut to hosts until the houses agree which claim to answer.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0104"><em>The three claimants</em>, 21 an Giblean, LE 552</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0105"></a>**20 an Cèitean, LE 553** — *Seann Warr shuts its gates* (Seann Warr). Seann Warr, the port nearest the capital on the west, shuts its gates to all three claimants and declares for none. Twice besieged in the war, it is taken by neither.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-4036"><em>Mairead nic Ruairidh bars the gate to all three</em>, 16 an t-Sultain, LE 552</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4037"></a>**10 an Dùbhlachd, LE 553** — *Seann Warr's first siege* (Seann Warr). Dùghall Garbh sits before Seann Warr a fortnight, cutting the eastern road, but its salt-pans and brine springs feed the town through the siege. Mairead nic Ruairidh sells his own host bread at the market rate until his carters cost him more than the town is worth, and he withdraws.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0105"><em>Seann Warr shuts its gates</em>, 20 an Cèitean, LE 553</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0106"></a>**22 an Gearran, LE 554** — *The ford at Àth shean* (Àth shean). The host of Dùghall Garbh meets that of Raghnall Ruadh at the ford of Àth shean and breaks it. The custody-book counts some three hundred dead, most of them drowned in the ford.
- <a id="ev-EIV-4038"></a>**25 am Màrt, LE 554** — *Dùghall crosses the shallows by night* (Àth shean). Guided by drovers who have used a hidden ford above Àth shean for forty years to move cattle untolled, Dùghall Garbh crosses his host in the dark and comes down on Raghnall Ruadh's camp from the landward side before dawn.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-III-0106"><em>The ford at Àth shean</em>, 22 an Gearran, LE 554</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4039"></a>**16 an t-Ògmhios, LE 554** — *Catrìona's answer to the ford* (Cathair dhomhain). Hearing word of Raghnall's breaking at the ford, Catrìona nic Aonghais sends Dùghall Garbh an answer naming no alliance: Cathair dhomhain holds for him, not for her, and she will not thank him for taking it from under her siege lines.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0106"><em>The ford at Àth shean</em>, 22 an Gearran, LE 554</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4040"></a>**14 an Dùbhlachd, LE 554** — *Coinneach mac Ailein's household flees Doire mhin* (Doire mhin). Woken by fire in the night, Coinneach mac Ailein carries his daughter Seònaid and the year's seed-corn out of the burning village of Doire mhin, while his wife brings the two younger children and the loosed cow finds its own way into the dark.
- <a id="ev-III-0107"></a>**24 an t-Sultain, LE 555** — *The burning of Doire mhin* (Doire mhin). Raghnall Ruadh's men in retreat burn the village of Doire mhin and its granary, to deny them to Dùghall. The villagers winter at Cathair mhòr on the charity of Macha's priests.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIV-4040"><em>Coinneach mac Ailein's household flees Doire mhin</em>, 14 an Dùbhlachd, LE 554</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4041"></a>**19 an t-Samhain, LE 555** — *The Doire mhin folk at Cathair mhòr* (Cathair mhòr). Forty-one burnt-out households of Doire mhin, walking six days south with what little they carried, are taken in at the temple of Macha in Cathair mhòr and fed through the winter on the temple's grain, without regard to whose claim they had favoured.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0107"><em>The burning of Doire mhin</em>, 24 an t-Sultain, LE 555</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4042"></a>**26 an t-Samhain, LE 556** — *Seann Warr's second siege* (Seann Warr). Dùghall Garbh, better provisioned than before, sits a full month before Seann Warr. The town holds again, though the winter comes on hard behind the siege, until word reaches Dùghall that Catrìona has closed both gates of Cathair dhomhain, and he marches east.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0105"><em>Seann Warr shuts its gates</em>, 20 an Cèitean, LE 553</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4043"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, LE 556** — *The water gate of Cathair dhomhain is closed* (Cathair dhomhain). On the counsel of a harbour-master of her following, Catrìona nic Aonghais sends borrowed fishing coasters onto the loch by night to shut Cathair dhomhain's water gate as her lines already hold the land gate, and the siege begins to starve the city in earnest.
- <a id="ev-EIV-4044"></a>**8 am Faoilleach, LE 557** — *The wells of Cathair dhomhain foul* (Cathair dhomhain). With no ground left beyond the walls to spare for burying, the dead of the siege lines are laid near the well-heads of Cathair dhomhain, and a sickness of the gut runs through the crowded streets and then through the garrison itself.
- <a id="ev-EIV-4045"></a>**11 an t-Sultain, LE 557** — *The garrison of Cathair dhomhain freed on oath* (Cathair dhomhain). Catrìona nic Aonghais takes the surrender of Niall Mòr mac Leòid on the fortieth day of the siege and lets his garrison march out between her silent lines, wounded and dead named and carried, on his sworn word not to take the field against her again.
- <a id="ev-III-0108"></a>**26 an Dùbhlachd, LE 557** — *The siege of Cathair dhomhain* (Cathair dhomhain). Catrìona nic Aonghais besieges Cathair dhomhain, which had declared for Dùghall, and takes it after forty days, when its wells are fouled by the dead of the siege lines. She lets the garrison go free on their oath.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-EIV-4039"><em>Catrìona's answer to the ford</em>, 16 an t-Ògmhios, LE 554</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-4043"><em>The water gate of Cathair dhomhain is closed</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, LE 556</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-4044"><em>The wells of Cathair dhomhain foul</em>, 8 am Faoilleach, LE 557</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIV-4045"><em>The garrison of Cathair dhomhain freed on oath</em>, 11 an t-Sultain, LE 557</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0109"></a>**24 am Faoilleach, LE 558** — *The hearths refused* (Muileann dhearg). Raghnall Ruadh, holding the vein-house, denies the measured handful of coal to every hearth and temple in the shires that stand against him. Hearths lit with the coal for generations go cold, and this deed turns more against him than any battle.
- <a id="ev-EIV-4501"></a>**27 an t-Iuchar, LE 558** — *The store-master's list* (Muileann dhearg). At Taigh na Fèithe Raghnall Ruadh hands the store-master Eòghann mac Dhùghaill a board naming every hearth and temple in the shires that stand against him and orders none of them measured a handful. The carriers who had come up the white road go down again with empty baskets.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-III-0109"><em>The hearths refused</em>, 24 am Faoilleach, LE 558</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4502"></a>**13 an Dàmhair, LE 558** — *The temple fires of the cold shires go out* (Cathair mhòr). Without the measured handful, hearths and temple fires across the shires that stood for Catrìona or Dùghall go grey through Dubhlas, among them the Macha temple at Cathair mhòr where the burned households of Doire mhin have wintered on charity, Seònaid nic Coinnich's family among them.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0109"><em>The hearths refused</em>, 24 am Faoilleach, LE 558</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4503"></a>**3 am Màrt, LE 559** — *The verse of the cold shires* (Cathair mhòr). A verse with no name to it goes about the cold shires that winter, sung over mended hearths and unmended ones alike: that no battle was lost, only the fire. It is remembered afterward as the first telling that named what Raghnall's refusal had done.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0109"><em>The hearths refused</em>, 24 am Faoilleach, LE 558</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4504"></a>**5 an Lùnastal, LE 559** — *The pact of Catrìona and Dùghall* (Cathair dhomhain). Dùghall Garbh comes to Catrìona nic Aonghais's camp with six men and no herald and offers to join their hosts against Raghnall Ruadh, saying that whichever of them wins the crown after this, it must not be a crown that can shut a door on a shire's hearths.
- <a id="ev-III-0110"></a>**14 am Faoilleach, LE 560** — *The battle of Muileann chrom* (Muileann chrom). The hosts of Catrìona and Dùghall, joined for the purpose, meet Raghnall Ruadh below Muileann chrom. Raghnall falls on the field, and the next day his own custodians open the vein-house.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-4504"><em>The pact of Catrìona and Dùghall</em>, 5 an Lùnastal, LE 559</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4505"></a>**18 am Màrt, LE 560** — *Taigh na Fèithe opened* (Muileann dhearg). The morning after Raghnall Ruadh falls at Muileann chrom, his own custodians strike the seal from the store without waiting to be told which claimant now holds the mountain, and the carriers go up the white road again.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-III-0110"><em>The battle of Muileann chrom</em>, 14 am Faoilleach, LE 560</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4506"></a>**15 an t-Sultain, LE 560** — *The first hearth relit* (Cathair mhòr). Word reaches Catrìona at Taigh na Fèithe that the temple fire at Cathair mhòr, built up all winter from borrowed turf and hedge-wood, has caught at last on coal from a carrier's basket, the first of the cold shires' hearths to burn again.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0110"><em>The battle of Muileann chrom</em>, 14 am Faoilleach, LE 560</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0111"></a>**16 an Dùbhlachd, LE 561** — *Death of Dùghall Garbh* (Baile Mòr dhomhain). Dùghall Garbh dies at Baile Mòr dhomhain of the wounds he took at Muileann chrom. His followers go over to Catrìona without further fighting.
- <a id="ev-EIV-4507"></a>**23 an Dùbhlachd, LE 561** — *Dùghall Garbh dies of his wound* (Baile Mòr dhomhain). Dùghall Garbh dies at Baile Mòr dhomhain of a cut taken below the arm at Muileann chrom that he hid from his own physicians for days. Catrìona nic Aonghais rides three days to reach him and finds him already dead, his last words asking only whether Taigh na Fèithe gates stood open.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-III-0111"><em>Death of Dùghall Garbh</em>, 16 an Dùbhlachd, LE 561</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4508"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, LE 561** — *Dùghall's captains come over unbidden* (Baile Mòr dhomhain). Dùghall Garbh's captains, led by Artair mac Lachlainn, come to Catrìona's camp within the fortnight and lay no terms before her, saying only that their dead lord had told them what he meant to do if the battle at Muileann chrom went their way, and that his word binds them still.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0111"><em>Death of Dùghall Garbh</em>, 16 an Dùbhlachd, LE 561</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0112"></a>**13 am Màrt, LE 562** — *Catrìona Bhuadhach crowned* (Cathair dhearg). Catrìona nic Aonghais is crowned at Cathair dhearg, and is known thereafter as Catrìona Bhuadhach. So ends the War of the Three Claimants, after some ten years.
- <a id="ev-EIV-4509"></a>**23 an Giblean, LE 562** — *Catrìona crowned at An Talla Dearg* (Cathair dhearg). Catrìona nic Aonghais is crowned at Cathair dhearg with little ceremony, the crown itself sent down under guard from Taigh na Fèithe's own custody. The seven heads swear to her in the old order, and she is called Catrìona Bhuadhach from that year.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-III-0112"><em>Catrìona Bhuadhach crowned</em>, 13 am Màrt, LE 562</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4510"></a>**19 an t-Sultain, LE 562** — *Eòghann keeps Raghnall's list unscraped* (Muileann dhearg). Eòghann mac Dhùghaill, still master of the store at Taigh na Fèithe, leaves Raghnall Ruadh's list of refused hearths standing face to the wall in the storeroom and sends word, unasked, that the store will not go a season again without measuring the handful while he holds the beam.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0109"><em>The hearths refused</em>, 24 am Faoilleach, LE 558</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0113"></a>**12 an Gearran, LE 565** — *The ruling of the hearth* (Muileann dhearg). Catrìona Bhuadhach and the vein-house set down in law that no claimant, house or king may withhold the measured handful from any lawful hearth. It is the first law written to bind the custodians themselves.
- <a id="ev-EIV-4511"></a>**23 an Gearran, LE 565** — *The drafting of Riaghailt an Teallaich* (Muileann dhearg). At Taigh na Fèithe's own yard Catrìona and the seven heads of the houses spend three days drafting one sentence binding any claimant, house or king from ever again withholding the measured handful. Eòghann mac Dhùghaill is called to testify what Raghnall Ruadh said to him, and his flat account settles the argument the queen's own words could not.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-III-0113"><em>The ruling of the hearth</em>, 12 an Gearran, LE 565</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4512"></a>**4 an t-Iuchar, LE 565** — *The seven heads set their marks* (Muileann dhearg). Riaghailt an Teallaich is entered into Leabhar a' Chùraim beside Lagh an Loscaidh Bhig in the same hand, and the seven heads of the houses set their marks to it one after another, Beathag nic Uisdein of Clann Ìomhair last and longest over her own mark.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0113"><em>The ruling of the hearth</em>, 12 an Gearran, LE 565</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4513"></a>**2 an t-Sultain, LE 565** — *Birth of Lachlann mac Iain* (Cathair dhearg). A son, Lachlann, is born at Cathair dhearg to Queen Catrìona Bhuadhach, nine-and-thirty years old and three years crowned, and her husband Iain mac Eachainn.
- <a id="ev-EIV-4514"></a>**14 an Dàmhair, LE 566** — *Seònaid nic Coinnich comes to An Talla Dearg* (Cathair dhearg). Seònaid nic Coinnich, whose father Coinneach mac Ailein came through the winter of the refusal with a cough he never lost, walks up from Cathair mhòr to An Talla Dearg and is taken into the queen's household as a clerk, the first of several children of the cold shires the household shelters in those years.
- <a id="ev-EIV-4515"></a>**1 an Giblean, LE 567** — *Seònaid copies the tallies of the refusal* (Cathair dhearg). In her first winter at An Talla Dearg, Seònaid nic Coinnich asks to see Leabhar a' Chùraim's oldest entries and copies out, unbidden, the tallies of the hearths refused in the winter of Na Teallaichean Fuara, a labour the queen never questions when she comes upon it by lamplight.
- <a id="ev-EIV-4516"></a>**11 an Dùbhlachd, LE 580** — *The council questions Rathad na Banrighinn* (Am Buabhall Fortanach). More than one head of house asks Catrìona in open council why she spends so much of the treasury on a stone road to her own town of Inis thais. She answers that a kingdom bound by a law written in a cold yard ought to be bound also by roads a hard winter cannot cut, and the building goes on.
- <a id="ev-III-0114"></a>**10 an Cèitean, LE 584** — *Catrìona's road south* (Am Buabhall Fortanach). Queen Catrìona has the road south from the capital by Baile shean and Am Buabhall Fortanach at Doire shean laid with stone, that her own town of Inis thais may be reached in any weather. It is called Rathad na Banrighinn.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-EIV-4516"><em>The council questions Rathad na Banrighinn</em>, 11 an Dùbhlachd, LE 580</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4517"></a>**1 an t-Sultain, LE 584** — *Rathad na Banrighinn laid to Inis thais* (Am Buabhall Fortanach). The stone of Rathad na Banrighinn is finished south from the capital, past Am Buabhall Fortanach at Doire shean, all the way to Catrìona's own gate at Inis thais, which she has ridden the length of twice while it was building to feel whether the stone held.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-III-0114"><em>Catrìona's road south</em>, 10 an Cèitean, LE 584</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4518"></a>**7 an Gearran, LE 585** — *The first carters run Rathad na Banrighinn* (Am Buabhall Fortanach). Salt-carts and grain-carts run the full length of the new stone road within the year the last stone is laid, cutting the journey from three days to two. An old carter tells the household he drove it half-blind and felt the cart go steady the whole way, a thing the mire road never let him do.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0114"><em>Catrìona's road south</em>, 10 an Cèitean, LE 584</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0115"></a>**11 an Giblean, LE 594** — *Seann Warr's gates honoured* (Seann Warr). In memory of its standing aside in the war, Queen Catrìona grants Seann Warr the right to keep its own gates and take its own tolls. The grant is cut over the landward gate.
- <a id="ev-EIV-4519"></a>**9 an Cèitean, LE 594** — *Death of Iain mac Eachainn* (Cathair dhearg). Iain mac Eachainn, the queen's husband, dies of a wasting in the chest no physician of the household can name. He had kept, through his years in An Talla Dearg, to the smaller business of the household and left the crown's affairs to Catrìona.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-III-0114"><em>Catrìona's road south</em>, 10 an Cèitean, LE 584</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4520"></a>**26 an t-Ògmhios, LE 594** — *Seann Warr's grant cut over the gate* (Seann Warr). In memory of its standing aside through the war and the two sieges it withstood, Catrìona grants Seann Warr the right to keep its own gates and take its own tolls, and the grant is cut in stone letters over the landward gate.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-III-0115"><em>Seann Warr's gates honoured</em>, 11 an Giblean, LE 594</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4521"></a>**26 an Dàmhair, LE 600** — *Birth of Anna* (Cathair dhearg). A daughter, Anna, is born at Cathair dhearg to Lachlann mac Iain, the queen's son, then five-and-thirty; the old queen, seventy-four, lives to see her granddaughter walk.

## The Years LE 601 – 700

- <a id="ev-EIV-4522"></a>**21 am Faoilleach, LE 602** — *Seònaid gathers the first three witnesses* (Cathair dhearg). At Queen Catrìona's own asking, her clerk Seònaid nic Coinnich takes down, in hurried hours snatched from the court's business, the first accounts of the war of the three claims: a soldier who fought at the ford, the son of Taigh na Fèithe's store-master, and a woman of Doire mhin who remembers Na Teallaichean Fuara as a child.
- <a id="ev-III-0116"></a>**7 an t-Iuchar, LE 604** — *Death of Catrìona Bhuadhach* (Cathair dhearg). Catrìona Bhuadhach dies at Cathair dhearg. Her son Lachlann mac Iain is crowned, and the houses swear to him in a single day, a thing the chroniclers remark on.
- <a id="ev-EIV-4523"></a>**19 an t-Iuchar, LE 604** — *Death of Catrìona Bhuadhach* (Cathair dhearg). Catrìona Bhuadhach dies at Cathair dhearg at seventy-eight, the last ruler to have fought in Cogadh nan Trì Tagraichean. Her son Lachlann mac Iain, not yet forty, succeeds her.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-III-0116"><em>Death of Catrìona Bhuadhach</em>, 7 an t-Iuchar, LE 604</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4524"></a>**29 an Dàmhair, LE 604** — *Na Seachd Taighean swear in a single day* (Cathair dhearg). The seven heads of the houses swear to Lachlann mac Iain within a single day of his mother's burial, Beathag nic Uisdein of Clann Ìomhair first to kneel. Seònaid nic Coinnich, watching from the back of the hall, counts the swearings without meaning to and goes that evening to begin the opening words of her history of the war.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0116"><em>Death of Catrìona Bhuadhach</em>, 7 an t-Iuchar, LE 604</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4525"></a>**19 an Gearran, LE 612** — *Seònaid visits the harbour-house boards* (Seann Skell). Carrying a grant of harbour dues she did not need to carry in her own hand, Seònaid nic Coinnich asks the harbour scribe Ailean mac Mhurchaidh to show her the old boards of Rolla nan Deònach, and rides home with an errand for herself she had not had when she set out.
- <a id="ev-EIV-4526"></a>**17 an Cèitean, LE 616** — *The store-master's board copied in full* (Muileann dhearg). Dòmhnall mac Eòghainn, who inherited his father Eòghann mac Dhùghaill's office at Taigh na Fèithe's store, lets Seònaid nic Coinnich copy in full the board of shires refused the coal in the year of Na Teallaichean Fuara, a board his father kept face to the wall and never scraped clean.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0109"><em>The hearths refused</em>, 24 am Faoilleach, LE 558</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4527"></a>**18 an Giblean, LE 618** — *The witness of Doire mhin heard in full* (Cathair mhòr). Seònaid nic Coinnich rides to Cathair mhòr to hear Mairead nic Aonghais, a woman of Doire mhin who was a child in the same charity and at the same temple as Seònaid herself, tell at length what a cold hearth was to a child too young to be told why it was cold.
- <a id="ev-EIV-4528"></a>**23 an Cèitean, LE 619** — *Seònaid weighs Leabhar a' Chùraim against her witnesses* (Muileann dhearg). At Taigh na Fèithe Seònaid nic Coinnich sets her gathered testimony against Leabhar a' Chùraim's own entries of the war, and finds days, numbers and causes of death the book and the witnesses do not agree on; she resolves to keep both accounts rather than choose between them.
- <a id="ev-EIV-4529"></a>**26 an t-Samhain, LE 619** — *Fearchar Ciar swears the ford broke on two days* (Muileann dhearg). Where Leabhar a' Chùraim gives the breaking at the ford of Àth shean as one day, the old soldier Fearchar Ciar swears to Seònaid nic Coinnich that it was two, the fighting taken up again at first light after a night neither side thought worth entering.<span class="fn fl">↩ Answers <a href="#ev-III-0106"><em>The ford at Àth shean</em>, 22 an Gearran, LE 554</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4530"></a>**21 an t-Ògmhios, LE 623** — *King Lachlann reads his mother into the book* (Cathair dhearg). Lachlann mac Iain finds Seònaid nic Coinnich at work on her history and asks whether it will say what his mother Catrìona was like; she answers that it will say what she did and what was believed of her, which is the most any book can give.
- <a id="ev-III-0117"></a>**8 an t-Ògmhios, LE 624** — *The Book of the Three Claimants* (Cathair dhearg). Seònaid nic Coinnich, once a clerk of Queen Catrìona's household, writes the story of the war from the custody-book and from the witness of those who fought. It is the oldest history of Dia-thìr that survives written as one tale and not as entries.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-4514"><em>Seònaid nic Coinnich comes to An Talla Dearg</em>, 14 an Dàmhair, LE 566</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-4515"><em>Seònaid copies the tallies of the refusal</em>, 1 an Giblean, LE 567</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-4522"><em>Seònaid gathers the first three witnesses</em>, 21 am Faoilleach, LE 602</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-4525"><em>Seònaid visits the harbour-house boards</em>, 19 an Gearran, LE 612</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-4527"><em>The witness of Doire mhin heard in full</em>, 18 an Giblean, LE 618</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-4528"><em>Seònaid weighs Leabhar a' Chùraim against her witnesses</em>, 23 an Cèitean, LE 619</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-4530"><em>King Lachlann reads his mother into the book</em>, 21 an t-Ògmhios, LE 623</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0118"></a>**3 an t-Sultain, LE 624** — *The sickness at Inis chrom* (Inis chrom). A spotted fever kills some forty at Inis chrom on the south-west coast. The Fianna of the Stone nurse the sick, and many of them die of it; thereafter the town is the Stone's.
- <a id="ev-EIV-4531"></a>**14 an t-Sultain, LE 624** — *Seònaid finishes Leabhar nan Trì Tagraichean* (Cathair dhearg). Seònaid nic Coinnich writes the last of the war's telling and sets down the finished leaves, the first history on Dia-thìr told as one tale from end to end rather than as separate entries.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-III-0117"><em>The Book of the Three Claimants</em>, 8 an t-Ògmhios, LE 624</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4532"></a>**6 an Giblean, LE 625** — *Leabhar nan Trì Tagraichean read at An Talla Dearg* (Cathair dhearg). King Lachlann mac Iain has Seònaid nic Coinnich's finished history read into the record at An Talla Dearg and orders it copied again and kept, ruling that no later copy of it may ever be made shorter than the one before it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0117"><em>The Book of the Three Claimants</em>, 8 an t-Ògmhios, LE 624</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-4533"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, LE 631** — *Death of Seònaid nic Coinnich* (Cathair dhearg). Seònaid nic Coinnich dies at Cathair dhearg at two-and-eighty, seven years after finishing her book, her last recorded word a complaint that the harbour-house's back room at Seann Skell wants a better roof before the damp takes its oldest boards.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0117"><em>The Book of the Three Claimants</em>, 8 an t-Ògmhios, LE 624</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0119"></a>**5 an Lùnastal, LE 634** — *The oyster beds of Doire shean* (Doire shean). Doire shean, a village on the southern shore, lays out oyster beds in its shallow bay and sends oysters by cart to the capital. The trade makes it rich enough to be a shire seat.
- <a id="ev-EIV-4534"></a>**7 an t-Iuchar, LE 635** — *Birth of the heir of Anna* (Cathair dhearg). A child is born at Cathair dhearg to Anna, Lachlann mac Iain's daughter, then five-and-thirty years old; Clàr nan Rìghrean keeps the year of the birth and lets the child's name fall from every copy that survives.
- <a id="ev-III-0119a"></a>**26 an Dàmhair, LE 644** — *The feast-market at Seann Tarr* (Seann Tarr). The crowds that come to the ancestor shrine at Seann Tarr for the great feasts begin to hold a market on the three feast days, chiefly of honey, beeswax for the shrine lights, and the dyes of Baile fhiadhaich. The wax lights of Seann Tarr are soon burned at ancestor shrines all along the north-eastern coast.
- <a id="ev-III-0120"></a>**1 an t-Sultain, LE 654** — *Manannan preached at Seann Skell* (Seann Skell). At Seann Skell, where the sting-creed of the Holy Age first called itself the only true one, the preacher Mànas mac Ruairidh proclaims its one power to be Manannan mac Lir, lord of the sea, whose Cup of Truth bears the yellow scorpion. He teaches that Manannan shut the eastern sea behind the fleet with his mist, which hides Dia-thìr from every ship beyond it, and that the crossing must not be tried again. His hearers are the first congregation of Òrd Mhanannain, the order of Manannan.
- <a id="ev-III-0121"></a>**30 an t-Sultain, LE 654** — *Death of Lachlann mac Iain* (Cathair dhearg). Lachlann mac Iain, son of Catrìona Bhuadhach, dies at Cathair dhearg, and his daughter Anna is crowned. The chroniclers call his reign quiet, and mean it as praise.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EIV-4513"><em>Birth of Lachlann mac Iain</em>, 2 an t-Sultain, LE 565</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EIV-4521"><em>Birth of Anna</em>, 26 an Dàmhair, LE 600</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIV-4534"><em>Birth of the heir of Anna</em>, 7 an t-Iuchar, LE 635</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-5001"></a>**26 an t-Samhain, LE 654** — *Ruairidh kneels first to Cupa na Fìrinne* (Seann Skell). At Seann Skell, Ruairidh, a sworn-man of the harbour-court, crosses the quay stones and kneels before his own son Mànas mac Ruairidh, the first of the preaching's hearers to do so. Six other net-menders kneel after him before the tide has gone out much further.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0120"><em>Manannan preached at Seann Skell</em>, 1 an t-Sultain, LE 654</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-5002"></a>**21 an Dùbhlachd, LE 654** — *Tidings of the king's death reach the quay* (Seann Skell). A rider watering his horse at Seann Skell's harbour-court brings word that Lachlann mac Iain has died at Cathair dhearg, eighty-nine years old after a reign of fifty quiet years, and that his daughter Anna, fifty-four, has been crowned in his place. Mànas mac Ruairidh is not recorded to have said anything of it.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-III-0121"><em>Death of Lachlann mac Iain</em>, 30 an t-Sultain, LE 654</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-5003"></a>**26 an Dùbhlachd, LE 655** — *The first boats blessed at Cidhe an Diosail* (Seann Skell). A dozen coasters are brought up one after another to Cidhe an Diosail at Seann Skell, and Mànas mac Ruairidh passes a plain wooden bowl of harbour water over each hull in turn, speaking the words that harden, within his own lifetime, into the fixed form of the rite of blessing.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0120"><em>Manannan preached at Seann Skell</em>, 1 an t-Sultain, LE 654</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-5004"></a>**9 an Dàmhair, LE 656** — *The harbour-court's scribe refuses the order's rite* (Seann Skell). Donnchadh mac Ailein, scribe of the harbour-court at Seann Skell, refuses to enter the blessings of Òrd Mhanannain in Rolla a' Chalaidh beside the tallies of hulls and cargoes, holding a rite to be no business of a board kept for hulls. Mànas does not press the matter.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0120"><em>Manannan preached at Seann Skell</em>, 1 an t-Sultain, LE 654</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0122"></a>**29 an Dàmhair, LE 674** — *Manannan's order at Ros bheag and Cuan shean* (Ros bheag). Fishing families carry the teaching of Manannan's order down the west coast to Ros bheag and Cuan shean. At Cuan shean the rope-makers are among the first to turn to it.
- <a id="ev-EIV-5005"></a>**31 an Dàmhair, LE 674** — *Tormod Ciar swears Cupa na Fìrinne on the rope-walk* (Cuan shean). At Cuan shean, the old rope-walker Tormod Ciar, told by a travelling net-mender what Mànas mac Ruairidh preaches of the mist, swears Cupa na Fìrinne before his fellow walkers on the rope-walk itself, cupping rainwater in his own hands for want of a bowl, with no priest of the order present to hear him.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0122"><em>Manannan's order at Ros bheag and Cuan shean</em>, 29 an Dàmhair, LE 674</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-5006"></a>**7 an t-Samhain, LE 680** — *Taigh Mhanannain raised at Seann Skell* (Seann Skell). Òrd Mhanannain raises its own house at Seann Skell, Taigh Mhanannain, low and built of the same grey stone as the quay near the old harbour-court. The congregation raises the silver for a proper cup without being asked, to replace the plain wooden bowl Mànas has used since the first blessing.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0120"><em>Manannan preached at Seann Skell</em>, 1 an t-Sultain, LE 654</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-5007"></a>**6 an Dùbhlachd, LE 680** — *Birth of the fifth ruler of the house of Catrìona* (Cathair dhearg). A child is born at Cathair dhearg to Anna's heir, then five-and-forty years old, in the six-and-twentieth year of Queen Anna's reign; Clàr nan Rìghrean keeps the year and not the name.
- <a id="ev-EIV-5008"></a>**27 an t-Sultain, LE 685** — *Death of Queen Anna* (Cathair dhearg). Queen Anna dies at Cathair dhearg at five-and-eighty, one-and-thirty years crowned, the last of the house of Catrìona whose name Clàr nan Rìghrean keeps for more than a century.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0121"><em>Death of Lachlann mac Iain</em>, 30 an t-Sultain, LE 654</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-5009"></a>**26 an Dàmhair, LE 685** — *The fourth ruler of the house of Catrìona crowned* (Cathair dhearg). Anna's heir is crowned at Cathair dhearg within the season, fifty years old. Clàr nan Rìghrean keeps the reign's years and not its name.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0121"><em>Death of Lachlann mac Iain</em>, 30 an t-Sultain, LE 654</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-5010"></a>**23 an Dùbhlachd, LE 690** — *Death of Mànas mac Ruairidh* (Seann Skell). Mànas mac Ruairidh dies at Seann Skell in the house he raised, six-and-thirty years after his first preaching on the quay, and is buried at his own asking under a plain slab facing the harbour mouth. Beathag nic Dhonnchaidh, who kept his house, keeps Taigh Mhanannain after him.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0120"><em>Manannan preached at Seann Skell</em>, 1 an t-Sultain, LE 654</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0123"></a>**27 an t-Samhain, LE 694** — *Within sight of land* (Ros bheag). The priests of Manannan at Ros bheag lay down that no boat of the faithful may go out of sight of the headlands. The rule is kept on the west coast for centuries, and steering by the stars, already half lost, is lost there wholly.
- <a id="ev-EIV-5011"></a>**30 an t-Samhain, LE 694** — *The rule of the headlands laid down* (Ros bheag). After a winter's debate, the priests of Òrd Mhanannain at Ros bheag lay down that no boat of the faithful may sail out of sight of the headlands, on pain of answering for it before Cupa na Fìrinne. The rule holds on the west coast far beyond any one preacher's lifetime.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-III-0123"><em>Within sight of land</em>, 27 an t-Samhain, LE 694</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-5012"></a>**5 an Dùbhlachd, LE 694** — *Coinneach mac Sheumais turned back within the year* (Ros bheag). Coinneach mac Sheumais, a skipper of Ros bheag, is turned back within the rule's first year by two of the order's own boats after taking his own boat further out than before, chasing a good run of fish. He never fishes so far out again.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0123"><em>Within sight of land</em>, 27 an t-Samhain, LE 694</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-5013"></a>**24 an t-Samhain, LE 698** — *Griogair cannot name his grandfather's star* (Ros bheag). A priest of Òrd Mhanannain at Ros bheag asks a boy named Griogair, grandson of one of the last pilots to hold a course by night on that shore, which star his grandfather steered by. The boy cannot answer, and no one in his own house had thought to write the star's name down.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0123"><em>Within sight of land</em>, 27 an t-Samhain, LE 694</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0124"></a>**19 an t-Ògmhios, LE 699** — *The granaries of Àth shean rebuilt* (Àth shean). The royal granaries at Àth shean, standing since before the Sundering, are pulled down and built again in stone on raised floors against the rats. The tally-house is rebuilt with them.
- <a id="ev-EIV-5014"></a>**2 an Dùbhlachd, LE 699** — *The granaries of Àth shean rebuilt* (Àth shean). The royal granaries at Àth shean, standing since before a' Scaradh, are pulled down and rebuilt in dressed stone on raised floors against the rats, along with a new tally-house. Fearchar mac Phàdraig, the reeve who oversees the three-year labour, sees the shire's grain stand dry through its first winter.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-III-0124"><em>The granaries of Àth shean rebuilt</em>, 19 an t-Ògmhios, LE 699</a>.</span>

## The Years LE 701 – 800

- <a id="ev-EIV-5015"></a>**27 an t-Sultain, LE 708** — *Murchadh Beag takes Eòghann mac Pheadair from the coal-face* (Muileann dhearg). The old scribe of Taigh na Fèithe, Murchadh Beag, hears a coal-breaker's young son recite back a whole day's cartage without once looking at the board, and asks the boy's father whether a household might spare him for a scribe's stool. Eòghann mac Pheadair is set to sweep Taigh na Fèithe floor and mix ink before he is let touch a leaf.
- <a id="ev-III-0125"></a>**24 am Faoilleach, LE 714** — *The rope-walks shortened* (Cuan shean). Cuan shean takes up half its rope-walks and sows the ground with barley. The rope trade had lived on the fleet and then on the fishing, and the fishing no longer needs rope of such length.
- <a id="ev-EIV-5016"></a>**30 an t-Iuchar, LE 714** — *Taigh na Fèithe's leaf takes in the rope-ground sown with barley* (Muileann dhearg). Eòghann mac Pheadair, fourteen and newly trusted with a leaf of his own, enters the ground given up by Cuan shean's rope-walks for barley, the first entry he copies whose full sense Murchadh Beag has to explain to him. He learns that a scribe's business is the fact and the year, not the grief behind it.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-III-0125"><em>The rope-walks shortened</em>, 24 am Faoilleach, LE 714</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-5017"></a>**31 an t-Iuchar, LE 722** — *Death of the fourth ruler of the house of Catrìona* (Cathair dhearg). The fourth ruler of the house of Catrìona dies at Cathair dhearg at seven-and-eighty after seven-and-thirty years crowned, and the heir, two-and-forty years old, is crowned the same season.
- <a id="ev-III-0126"></a>**22 an Gearran, LE 724** — *Wave at Cnoc chaol* (Cnoc chaol). A great swell with no storm behind it runs up the beach at Cnoc chaol on the south coast and carries off the drying racks and two children. The village sets its racks higher up the shore.
- <a id="ev-EIV-5018"></a>**11 an t-Iuchar, LE 724** — *Eòghann mac Pheadair at four-and-twenty* (Muileann dhearg). At four-and-twenty Eòghann mac Pheadair has old Murchadh Beag's stool at Taigh na Fèithe as good as his own, and enters the wave at Cnoc chaol on the general leaf as he enters every disaster that touches a household of the coal-right: names, place, day.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0126"><em>Wave at Cnoc chaol</em>, 22 an Gearran, LE 724</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-5019"></a>**10 an t-Sultain, LE 725** — *A household of Cnoc chaol removes its gallery-claim from the shore* (Cnoc chaol). After the great wave that took two children from the beach at Cnoc chaol, the household of one of the drowned strikes itself from its old gallery and takes up a new claim further from the water. Eòghann mac Pheadair enters the removal on Taigh na Fèithe's leaf the following season, cold and plain as he was taught.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0126"><em>Wave at Cnoc chaol</em>, 22 an Gearran, LE 724</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0126a"></a>**11 an t-Samhain, LE 731** — *The market of the eastern road* (Baile Mòr dhìreach). Baile Mòr dhìreach, the citadel on the straight eastern road, is granted a market for the east coast. There the fish and sail-cloth of the coast towns meet the furs, hides and dyes of the hills, and the dyers of Baile Mòr ruadh sell their colours nowhere else.
- <a id="ev-EIV-5020"></a>**23 an Dùbhlachd, LE 731** — *Eòghann mac Pheadair witnesses the market bounds at Baile Mòr dhìreach* (Baile Mòr dhìreach). Sent east on his own feet for the first time, Eòghann mac Pheadair stands witness for Na Seachd Taighean when the crown's grant of a market is read at Baile Mòr dhìreach and its boundary stones set. He watches the first stalls go up the same afternoon and walks the road home slower than he walked out.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-III-0126a"><em>The market of the eastern road</em>, 11 an t-Samhain, LE 731</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-5021"></a>**10 an t-Samhain, LE 738** — *Mòrag nic Ìomhair rides to Taigh na Fèithe with the crown's leaves* (Muileann dhearg). A scribe of An Talla Dearg's own household, Mòrag nic Ìomhair, rides the thirty-nine miles to Taigh na Fèithe at Muileann dhearg to set the crown's reckoning of Bliadhnaichean an Diosail against Leabhar a' Chùraim's own, after the two offices' counts are found not to agree. The master of Taigh na Fèithe grants her the book for as many days as the matter takes.
- <a id="ev-EIV-5022"></a>**9 an Dùbhlachd, LE 738** — *The fault in the count is found and cannot be mended* (Muileann dhearg). Working three days by lamplight, Eòghann mac Pheadair and Mòrag nic Ìomhair trace the two offices' counts of An Diosal back to a single year, early after An Diosal, entered twice by one office's habit or once by the other's. Neither leaf either scribe has brought can say which office erred, or whether either truly has.
- <a id="ev-III-0127"></a>**23 am Màrt, LE 739** — *The two counts reconciled* (Muileann dhearg). The vein-house and the crown's scribes find that their counts of years since the Setting-Out differ, and settle the difference by agreement. The same agreement fixes the day of the rite of the empty harbour, which each count had placed otherwise; later scribes cease to pretend it was fixed by proof.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-5021"><em>Mòrag nic Ìomhair rides to Taigh na Fèithe with the crown's leaves</em>, 10 an t-Samhain, LE 738</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIV-5022"><em>The fault in the count is found and cannot be mended</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, LE 738</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-5023"></a>**7 an t-Iuchar, LE 739** — *The two counts settled by agreement, not by proof* (Muileann dhearg). Taigh na Fèithe and the crown's scribe take the crown's count for the reckoning that will go forward, since it touches more households than Taigh na Fèithe's own, and Eòghann mac Pheadair writes Taigh na Fèithe's agreement to it in his own hand. The master of Taigh na Fèithe's mark is set under his, and the crown scribe's office mark under that.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0127"><em>The two counts reconciled</em>, 23 am Màrt, LE 739</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-5024"></a>**7 an Lùnastal, LE 739** — *The day of Deas-ghnàth a' Chalaidh Fhalaimh fixed* (Seann Skell). The same agreement that settles the count also fixes, for the first time, a single day on which Deas-ghnàth a' Chalaidh Fhalaimh is to be kept by every harbour of the coast together, in place of each keeping it a day or two either side of its neighbours by its own old custom. Mòrag nic Ìomhair carries word of it down to Seann Skell.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0127"><em>The two counts reconciled</em>, 23 am Màrt, LE 739</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-5025"></a>**12 an t-Sultain, LE 739** — *The agreement-leaf folded into Leabhar a' Chùraim* (Muileann dhearg). Eòghann mac Pheadair keeps his copy of the sealed agreement between two older leaves of Leabhar a' Chùraim that had never before had a stranger's mark folded in among them. He tells the master of Taigh na Fèithe only that the crown's scribe was a hard woman to argue a figure past and an easy one to agree a figure with.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0127"><em>The two counts reconciled</em>, 23 am Màrt, LE 739</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-5026"></a>**6 am Màrt, LE 740** — *The coast keeps the rite on the agreed day* (Muileann dhearg). Mòrag nic Ìomhair writes to Eòghann mac Pheadair the following winter that not a single harbour of the coast has written to complain of the day set for Deas-ghnàth a' Chalaidh Fhalaimh. Eòghann keeps the short note folded inside his own working leaves for the rest of his working life.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0127"><em>The two counts reconciled</em>, 23 am Màrt, LE 739</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-5027"></a>**15 am Faoilleach, LE 751** — *Birth of Eilidh Bhàn* (Cathair dhearg). A girl, Eilidh, fair enough to be called Eilidh Bhàn from her first year, is born at Cathair dhearg, granddaughter of the ruler who has then held the hall nine-and-twenty years.
- <a id="ev-EIV-5028"></a>**27 an Lùnastal, LE 762** — *Word of the disputation at Inis mhòr reaches Taigh na Fèithe* (Muileann dhearg). A rider carries north country talk to Taigh na Fèithe of a house of disputation newly founded at Inis mhòr, whose first master refuses every answer offered him on whether the vein answers any true count of years or only the custom of counting it. Eòghann mac Pheadair, old now, hears it out and goes back to his leaf.
- <a id="ev-III-0128"></a>**12 am Faoilleach, LE 769** — *The druid school at Inis mhòr* (Inis mhòr). Pupils of Dùn thais found a house of disputation at Inis mhòr, and the question of the vein is argued in the north for the first time. Its first master, Fionnlagh mac Aonghais, is remembered for refusing every answer offered him.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-EIV-5028"><em>Word of the disputation at Inis mhòr reaches Taigh na Fèithe</em>, 27 an Lùnastal, LE 762</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0129"></a>**10 an Gearran, LE 769** — *Queen Eilidh Bhàn crowned* (Cathair dhearg). Eilidh Bhàn, sixth ruler of the house of Catrìona, is crowned at Cathair dhearg, a girl of eighteen. The annals of her long reign are almost wholly of harvests.<span class="fn fl">◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EIV-5007"><em>Birth of the fifth ruler of the house of Catrìona</em>, 6 an Dùbhlachd, LE 680</a>; → Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-5017"><em>Death of the fourth ruler of the house of Catrìona</em>, 31 an t-Iuchar, LE 722</a>; ◇ Same person <a href="#ev-EIV-5027"><em>Birth of Eilidh Bhàn</em>, 15 am Faoilleach, LE 751</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0130"></a>**22 an Gearran, LE 769** — *The bath-house at the hot springs* (Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh). Clann Choinnich rebuilds in dressed stone the old bath-house over the hot springs of Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh, and admits the sick of any house one day in seven. Its physicians keep a book of cures, afterwards lost.
- <a id="ev-EIV-5029"></a>**9 am Màrt, LE 769** — *The master of Taigh na Fèithe stands for Eòghann at the crowning* (Muileann dhearg). When Na Seachd Taighean' custodians go down to Cathair dhearg to see the new queen crowned, as the compact requires, the master of Taigh na Fèithe goes in place of Eòghann mac Pheadair, whose legs will no longer answer for a journey of thirty-nine miles in a single season. Eòghann hears the crowning described to him afterward by the returning master.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-III-0129"><em>Queen Eilidh Bhàn crowned</em>, 10 an Gearran, LE 769</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-5030"></a>**2 an Giblean, LE 769** — *Eòghann mac Pheadair is carried to the bath-house at Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh* (Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh). In the last cold turn of the year, his chest gone tight in a way no winter before has managed, Eòghann mac Pheadair lets himself be carried by cart to the rebuilt bath-house below Muileann ruadh, where he sits in the warm water among coal-breakers, salt-carriers and a shepherd's widow, none of them minding whose gallery the others answer to.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-III-0130"><em>The bath-house at the hot springs</em>, 22 an Gearran, LE 769</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-5031"></a>**28 an Giblean, LE 769** — *Eòghann mac Pheadair shows the agreement-leaf to his own pupil* (Muileann dhearg). Asked by the young scribe he has lately taken to teaching what the finest thing was that he ever did in a life spent mostly at a stool, Eòghann mac Pheadair unfolds the thirty-year-old agreement-leaf and tells the boy it was not the count that made it worth keeping, but the honest agreement written under it.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-III-0127"><em>The two counts reconciled</em>, 23 am Màrt, LE 739</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-5032"></a>**6 an t-Sultain, LE 769** — *Death of the fifth ruler of the house of Catrìona* (Cathair dhearg). The fifth ruler of the house of Catrìona dies at Cathair dhearg at nine-and-eighty after seven-and-forty years crowned, and the crown passes to a granddaughter, Eilidh Bhàn, eighteen years old.<span class="fn fl">→ Leads to <a href="#ev-III-0129"><em>Queen Eilidh Bhàn crowned</em>, 10 an Gearran, LE 769</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-5033"></a>**12 an Dàmhair, LE 782** — *A coaster boarded off the small islands* (Baile chrom). A coaster out of Ros bheag puts in at Baile chrom two days late and a third short in her hold, her skipper telling Coinneach mac Nèill, the reeve, that three boats out of the small islands boarded her and took her grain, wearing no mark and hiding no face.
- <a id="ev-III-0131"></a>**24 am Faoilleach, LE 784** — *The sea-thieves of the north-west* (Spùinneadairean-mara). Boats out of the small islands off the north-west coast begin to rob the coasting traders of fish and grain. The sea-thieves are Dia-thìrich, men of the north-west shore, and the harbour rolls name some of them.<span class="fn fl">← Leads to <a href="#ev-EIV-5033"><em>A coaster boarded off the small islands</em>, 12 an Dàmhair, LE 782</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-5034"></a>**26 an Gearran, LE 784** — *Rolla a' Chalaidh name Aonghas mac Ruairidh among the sea-thieves* (Baile chrom). The first full count of the takings sent up to Cathair dhearg names, among the sea-thieves of the small islands, a fisherman's son of Baile chrom, Aonghas mac Ruairidh. His mother tells the reeve plainly that a young man who watches the fish thin will go looking for a living wherever it is still to be found.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0131"><em>The sea-thieves of the north-west</em>, 24 am Faoilleach, LE 784</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-III-0132"></a>**26 an Dùbhlachd, LE 789** — *Baile chrom half empty* (Baile chrom). The reeve of Baile chrom on the north-west coast reports half the houses of the town empty, their families gone east before the sea-thieves and the poor harvests. The crown remits the town's grain dues.
- <a id="ev-EIV-5035"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, LE 789** — *Half of Baile chrom stands empty* (Baile chrom). Coinneach mac Nèill reports to the crown's scribes that half the houses of Baile chrom stand empty, their families gone inland before the sea-thieves and the failing catch, their thatch going to moss and their doors shut on rooms no one will sleep in again that year.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0132"><em>Baile chrom half empty</em>, 26 an Dùbhlachd, LE 789</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-5036"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, LE 789** — *Baile chrom's grain dues remitted* (Baile chrom). The crown remits Baile chrom's grain dues to a sum reckoned by the households that stand rather than the households that once stood, answering Coinneach mac Nèill's plain report with a plain word of thanks for a count taken with care.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0132"><em>Baile chrom half empty</em>, 26 an Dùbhlachd, LE 789</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-5037"></a>**5 an Gearran, LE 790** — *Birth of Dòmhnall Ruadh*. A son, red-haired and called Dòmhnall Ruadh, is born at Muileann chrom to a custodian household of Clann Raghnaill that keeps three galleries under the mountain and has never once been asked into An Talla Dearg except to petition.
- <a id="ev-EIV-5038"></a>**18 an Lùnastal, LE 795** — *The reeve's letter asking for a force* (Baile chrom). After the sea-thieves put in twice within a single moon on strands within sight of his own harbour, Coinneach mac Nèill writes to the crown asking not for lightened dues this time but for an armed force, since a reeve with a tally-stick can no longer hold a coast his own shire's desperate sons have made their hunting ground.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0132"><em>Baile chrom half empty</em>, 26 an Dùbhlachd, LE 789</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-5039"></a>**4 an Giblean, LE 800** — *Iain mac Thormoid raised against the small islands* (Baile chrom). Eilidh Bhàn raises a force under a captain named Iain mac Thormoid and sends it north by sea to Baile chrom, answering the reeve's long-waited letter. The captain charts the raiders' ground on Coinneach mac Nèill's own table with the help of the town's fishermen before the boats sail against the small islands.

## The Years LE 801 – 900

- <a id="ev-III-0133"></a>**27 an t-Samhain, LE 801** — *The raid on Eilean dhubh* (Eilean dhubh). A force sent by Queen Eilidh Bhàn lands on Eilean dhubh and burns the sea-thieves' boats on the strand. Their leader, Uilleam Ruadh, is taken to Cathair dhearg and hanged.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EIV-5039"><em>Iain mac Thormoid raised against the small islands</em>, 4 an Giblean, LE 800</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-5040"></a>**6 an Dùbhlachd, LE 801** — *Creach Eilean dhubh* (Eilean dhubh). Iain mac Thormoid's boats land at first light on Eilean dhubh and burn the sea-thieves' hulls on the strand, Coinneach mac Nèill's own fishermen leading the way through the channel among the small islands. The sea-thieves, unwatched for the better part of a decade, are taken all but by surprise.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0133"><em>The raid on Eilean dhubh</em>, 27 an t-Samhain, LE 801</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-5041"></a>**11 an Dùbhlachd, LE 801** — *Aonghas mac Ruairidh dies on the strand* (Eilean dhubh). Aonghas mac Ruairidh, thirty-one years old and once a boy Coinneach mac Nèill carried on his own shoulder to this same water, is killed defending a hull on Eilean dhubh's strand. The reeve kneels over him and finds he has no words ready for the mother he must tell of it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-III-0133"><em>The raid on Eilean dhubh</em>, 27 an t-Samhain, LE 801</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EIV-5042"></a>**19 an Dùbhlachd, LE 801** — *Uilleam Ruadh taken and hanged* (Cathair dhearg).
